screening_results.reason: The article describes development and validation of an image database and selection of image sets and Psychopy code for fMRI tasks, but it does not report any human fMRI data, task-evoked whole-brain analyses, or within-participant contrasts of drug cues>control. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI study), I4 (within-participant contrast drug>control), I5/I6 (whole-brain task activation maps). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cannabis cues in adolescents and reports within-subject contrasts (cannabis > non-cannabis). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FLAME; cluster-corrected Z thresholds) and results are reported across whole-brain clusters. Key methodological details required by the review (participant age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, processing software FSL) are provided. The study does not violate any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes an unmasked whole-brain task effect). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

Although this study is an fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual drug (cocaine) and neutral videos (satisfying I3), the provided full text reports only subjective craving outcomes and does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or activation contrasts (drug>control). No voxelwise results, coordinate tables, figures, or whole-brain analyses are described. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task activation evidence (I5/I4). As such, it should be excluded under the review exclusion criteria for studies lacking whole-brain results.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (cocaine vs neutral pictures) in recently abstinent cocaine-dependent participants. It includes a within-participant contrast (cocaine > neutral) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (one-sample t tests for the cocaine>neutral contrast, with voxel- and cluster-level corrected results and supplementary tables). Relevant methodological details are reported (participant age and sex, cue type: cocaine, scanner: 3T, software: SPM8). The paper also reports additional connectivity analyses but does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity results. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cue-reactivity using visual drug-related stimuli (alcohol- and cannabis-related words). Participants performed an addiction-Stroop task with within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral color, cannabis > neutral color) and first-level contrasts were carried to group-level random-effects analyses. The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with cluster-level correction and report significant clusters and brain–behavior correlations (i.e., qualifying whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures). Key participant demographic details (age/sex counts), cue types (alcohol, cannabis), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) in adolescents. The study reports within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > neutral cues and conducts second-level, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (thresholds and cluster criteria reported). Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue paradigms (pictures) for drug (cocaine) and natural reward (food) cues, reporting within-participant contrasts (cocaine vs neutral; food vs neutral). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds reported) and presents cluster results and figures; processing software (SPM) and participant demographics (age, sex, BMI) are provided. MRI protocol is described in the Supplement (acceptable per inclusion rules). Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual food cue-reactivity (natural reward). It reports within-subject contrasts (high-calorie > low-calorie foods), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests and multiple regression), and reports coordinates and cluster results. Necessary methodological details are provided (participant age and sex: females 18–35; cue type: food; MRI field strength: 3T; processing software: SPM12/MATLAB). Results include whole-brain activations and small-volume corrected amygdala findings, satisfying reporting requirements. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and conclusions. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of tobacco (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) in smokers and matched non-smokers. The design includes within-participant contrasts of craving (Cr) and aversion (Av) pictures versus control mosaic scenes, and group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses with voxelwise inference (FDR thresholds reported). Results are reported as whole-brain activations (regions/BA, p-values) and correlations with behavioral measures. The manuscript reports participant sex (male), describes age-matched groups, cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study examined nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli and within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts, but the cue-reactivity results are reported using a priori ROIs (four insula subregions and two ACC ROIs) and subsequent ROI-based beta extractions and regressions. No group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or whole-brain task results are reported in the provided full text; task analyses focus on ROI beta weights and resting-state connectivity. Therefore it qualifies as an ROI-only task analysis and meets exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI visual drug cue reactivity) and I4 (within-participant drug>control contrast) but I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met.

This is an fMRI study using visual cues (drug and food videos) to assess cue-reactivity in cocaine-dependent and control participants. It reports within-participant contrasts (DRUG vs FOOD), group-level whole-brain task analyses (flexible factorial Group x VideoType interaction) with cluster coordinates and ROI small-volume corrections, and provides participant age/sex, cue types (cocaine, food), scanner field strength (3T Siemens TrioTim), and processing software (SPM12). Thus it meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI cue-reactivity with visual stimuli, provides a within-subject contrast of cue types, reports whole-brain group-level results (tables/coordinates/supplement), and includes required participant and acquisition details.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images). The authors computed within-participant contrasts comparing trials containing a smoking image versus two neutral images (beta maps), used these in MVPA, and performed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (accuracy maps warped to MNI space and tested with cluster correction), reporting significant clusters/coordinates and describing results in the text. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and software (SPM8, AFNI, FSL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli with a within-subject alcohol vs neutral contrast (I3, I4) and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (I7), the paper’s primary results are ROI-to-ROI gPPI connectivity analyses. The report does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain voxelwise activation results (only ROI-based connectivity findings). This violates the requirement for a whole-brain task activation analysis (I5). Therefore the study must be excluded under exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity-only analyses without whole-brain task maps). Full text appears complete.

This study is an empirical BOLD fMRI investigation of visual smoking (nicotine) cues using a within-subject cue-reactivity task (smoking-related images vs. neutral images). The authors report within-participant contrasts (smoking cue > neutral) and conduct group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster- and familywise-error correction, presenting significant clusters and extracted percent signal change. The manuscript reports participant age and sex distribution, cue type (nicotine), MRI scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual heroin cue videos and within-participant drug cue > neutral contrasts, but the reported analyses are ROI-based time-course and correlational analyses. The manuscript does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps, coordinate tables, or whole-brain results in the text or figures. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, with within-subject contrasts comparing food>non-food, and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (whole-brain FWE-corrected activations reported). Methods report scanner field strength (3T), processing software (SPM12), and participant age/sex. Imaging data are available online (NeuroVault) and results include voxelwise analyses and coordinate reporting. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study used auditory guided-imagery (personalized audiotaped scripts) rather than visual cue stimuli. The meta-analysis specifically requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3). Although the study includes within-participant contrasts (favorite-food vs neutral), whole-brain group-level analyses, and reports relevant participant and MRI details, it does not meet I3 and therefore does not qualify for inclusion.

The study uses personalized audio-guided imagery (auditory cues) of favorite foods rather than visual stimuli. Inclusion criterion I3 requires cue-reactivity assessed using visual stimuli; this study therefore does not meet I3. The study does include within-participant contrasts of favorite-food cue > control and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results and participant/cue/scanner details, so I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on failure to meet the modality requirement (visual stimuli).

This study reports an empirical fMRI experiment using visual alcohol-associated cues in abstinent alcoholics and controls. It includes a within-participant contrast comparing alcohol-associated versus abstract/control stimuli, and reports group-level, voxelwise analyses conducted with SPM99 (fixed-effects group analysis) and whole-brain BOLD results (regions activated are described). Relevant participant information (ages, sex distribution), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM99) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods (psychophysiology and fMRI acquisition/analysis), results, and discussion, so the core article content is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without an unmasked task effect, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the paper satisfies all required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

Although this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of cannabis using visual stimuli with a within-subject cannabis cue > appetitive cue contrast and reports participant demographics and scanner/software details, the paper reports ROI-based analyses (mean z-statistics extracted from a priori anatomical masks) and does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinate tables/figures for whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videotaped cues). The paper reports within-subject contrasts including cigarette cues > neutral (cigarette cue crave vs neutral and cigarette cue resist vs neutral, and direct contrasts between cue conditions). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were performed using FSL/FEAT with cluster correction (Z>2.3, p=0.01) and results are described in the text (with coordinate-based clusters), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This article is a narrative review rather than an empirical fMRI study. The full text summarizes theoretical and animal research and discusses fMRI and phMRI applications, but it contains no original human fMRI methods, participant data, task contrasts (e.g., within-participant cue>control contrasts), whole-brain statistical maps, or reported coordinates. Therefore it does not meet the review’s requirement for original, whole-brain task-evoked fMRI data and meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original human fMRI data). The provided full text appears complete (introduction, discussion, conclusions); however, no primary fMRI results are reported.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cannabis cue-reactivity using visual/tactile cues and reports seed-based PPI (functional connectivity) and Granger (effective connectivity) results comparing cannabis vs neutral cues. However, the paper does not report a univariate, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map for drug cues > control stimuli (only seed-based connectivity/effective connectivity results are presented). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only seed-based/effective connectivity without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual alcohol-related word cues (visual stimuli) and neutral word controls. The analysis includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol>neutral (fit coefficients contrasting conditions) and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical tests (independent-samples t tests and single-sample t tests performed for each voxel, with AFNI and cluster correction reported). Participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner parameters and processing software (AFNI) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cannabis cue reactivity using visual stimuli (images of cannabis, cigarettes, neutral, and animals). It includes within-subject contrasts (Can > Neutral and Can > Neutral + Cigarette). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FEAT, 2×2 ANOVA with random effects) and provides cluster results with peak MNI coordinates. Participant age/sex, cue type (cannabis/cigarette), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (fMRIPrep, FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) are violated. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of opioid cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (opioid words). It includes within-participant contrasts (opioid-word vs. neutral-word, OW>NW) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM second-level analyses (one-sample and two-sample t-tests) used to define activations. Methods report participant demographics, cue type (opioid words), MRI scanner field strength (3T Philips), and processing software (AFNI for despiking, SPM12 for preprocessing and analysis). Although the paper also includes connectivity (DCM) analyses, univariate whole-brain task activation maps are reported and described, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This study examines fMRI cue-reactivity to visual food cues (natural reward) and includes within-subject food>neutral contrasts and reports participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, analyses are conducted using a priori ROI masks (AAL) and report ROI-based results; the paper does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). The full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual stimuli (cocaine-related pictures vs natural scenes) and includes within-participant contrasts of cocaine>control stimuli. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (FSL GLM, Randomise, whole-brain thresholding), with results described in text and figures/tables. Participant demographics (male, mean age 56.5), cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (3T Siemens), and processing software (FSL) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling assessment. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (shapes) in a monetary incentive delay task assessing neural responses to natural reward-related cues (money). It includes within-subject contrasts of reward cues > nonincentive cues and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected maps and peak coordinates. Participant demographics, cue type (monetary), 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (AFNI) are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity that used visual cues (abstract shapes predicting beer vs water) and included within-subject contrasts (beer>water) for anticipation/outcome/delivery phases. The authors report group-level, whole-brain one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs for the beer>water contrasts (with thresholding and coordinates), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The manuscript provides participant age/sex (male, ages 18–25), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T Prisma), and processing software (SPM8), and reports results in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (cocaine videos) and an appetitive visual control (food videos), with within-subject contrasts separating cocaine versus food cue responses (hierarchical regression isolating cocaine>food variance). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses are reported (whole-brain contrasts, cluster thresholds, and stereotaxic coordinates/BA results described). Relevant methodological details are provided: cue types (cocaine and food), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (AFNI); participants are described as gender- and age-matched (participant counts provided). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of alcohol (drug) and food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual cues (500 ms cue symbols). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., high-threat alcohol cues vs high-threat food/neutral cues) and task-evoked analyses. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (AFNI 3dMVM, cluster correction via 3dClustSim) with results described in the text and referenced figures/tables. Necessary metadata are provided: participant demographics (age/sex), cue types (alcohol, food, neutral), scanner field strength (Siemens Prisma 3T), and processing software (AFNI). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues with within-subject contrasts (drug > neutral), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8, AlphaSim correction) and reported relevant participant and scanning information (male participants, matched by age, heroin cue type, 3.0T scanner, SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual stimuli (e-cigarette and neutral videos) to assess cue-reactivity in experienced e-cigarette users. The analyses include within-participant contrasts of e-cigarette vs neutral videos (video condition main effect and session x video interaction) at the group level using a voxelwise repeated-measures ANOVA with cluster-level correction; whole-brain results are reported (including Talairach coordinates). The manuscript reports participant age range and demographic details, cue type (nicotine/e-cigarette), scanner field strength (3T Siemens), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses visual alcohol cues within a hybrid task and reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol versus neutral/scrambled images. Second-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM8 with cluster/FWE correction and resulting clusters/coordinates are reported. Relevant metadata are provided (participant ages range, sex noted, cue type = alcohol, 3T scanner, SPM8 preprocessing). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward stimuli (infant faces/baby schema) in opioid use disorder patients, with within-subject contrasts (Low/Unmanipulated/High baby schema vs crosshair and High vs Low), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded and cluster-corrected) reported. Participant age/sex, cue type (infant faces), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and neutral control images, reporting within-participant (heroin > neutral) contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with thresholding and cluster reporting. Participant demographics (male, age range 18–55), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (1.5 T Philips), and processing software are reported. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual drug-cue reactivity.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) visual cue-reactivity with an within-subject smoking>neutral contrast and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results (tables/Supplement). It therefore meets I3, I4, I5, and I6. However the full text provided does not report MRI scanner field strength (e.g., 1.5T/3T) and does not give explicit participant age range (only "college students") in the main text; inclusion criterion I7 requires reporting of participant age and sex, cue type, MRI scanner field strength, and processing software. Processing software (FSL), cue type (nicotine), and sex (male) are reported, but MRI field strength and clear age information are not. Because not all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I7 missing), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual beverage photographs embedded as distractors. The authors report within-participant contrasts comparing alcohol distractors vs. non-alcohol distractors (AD > NAD/AD-NAD), and perform group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (rmANOVA and voxelwise correlations) with multiple-comparison correction. Methods report MRI field strength (3T) and processing software (AFNI, SPM5), and participant age and sex distributions are described. Whole-brain results are described and thresholded (FWE-corrected clusters), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effects, empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues with an explicit within-subject contrast (Alcohol>Neutral) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses. The paper reports whole-brain results (both ROI-corrected and exploratory whole-brain mappings) and provides coordinates/figures, fulfilling the requirement that whole-brain task-evoked maps are available. Necessary methodological details are reported (cue type: alcohol visual stimuli; scanner field strength: 3T; processing software: SPM8), and participant demographics and sex matching are described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli in active cocaine users, with within-subject contrasts comparing cocaine-related vs neutral backgrounds. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps were computed and thresholded (voxelwise t, cluster correction) and reported in the results (clusters/ROIs), meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Methods report scanner field strength (3T General Electric Signa) and processing software (AFNI), and participant age/sex and cue type (cocaine) are detailed. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for visual drug cue-reactivity fMRI and reports necessary methodological details.

This study is a task-based fMRI cue-reactivity investigation using visual alcohol cues (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage images) with a within-participant contrast (alcoholic cues > non-alcoholic cues). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were conducted (one-sample t-test, voxel-level thresholds reported) with coordinates and region-level results provided. Key methodological details required by the review are reported: participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-related cues and neutral controls, reporting within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs neutral) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2). The paper provides participant age and sex (male, ages reported), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM2). Whole-brain results and coordinates are reported; small-volume correction was also used for a priori VOIs but whole-brain voxelwise analyses and between-group tests are present. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is original human fMRI task activation data).

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual methamphetamine and sexual images in human participants (men aged 19–45). It reports within-subject contrasts (methamphetamine>neutral; sexual>neutral and sexual>methamphetamine) and group-level mixed-effects analyses. The paper includes whole-brain, voxelwise results (cluster peak coordinates, F-statistic, cluster size, and p-value for the left superior frontal cortex), and describes whole-brain correction thresholds and SPM12 processing on a 3.0-T scanner. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, scanner field strength, and processing software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used visual heroin-related and pleasant (natural reward) images in an abstinent opioid-dependent and control sample. It reports within-subject contrasts (heroin vs baseline/neutral; pleasant vs baseline), and group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (results reported with coordinates and FDR-corrected thresholds). Key methodological details are provided (participant age/sex, cue types, 3T scanner field strength, SPM2 processing). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full-text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of cigarettes vs neutral pens) presented alongside partner/acquaintance images. The study reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., acquaintance+cigarette vs acquaintance+pen; partner+cigarette vs partner+pen) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction (AFNI). Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a visual alcohol cue-reactivity task (alcohol vs neutral pictures) with within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM, cluster correction via AlphaSim) and results are described with cluster-level findings; participant age range, gender, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T Siemens), and processing software (SPM) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for visual drug-cue fMRI whole-brain task activation reporting.

Although this is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli with within-participant alcohol>neutral contrasts (meets I3 and I4), the report presents only anatomically- and functionally-defined ROI analyses and striatum-masked voxelwise results. The paper does not report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map required by I5. Therefore it falls under exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). The full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual smoking cues (hand holding a cigarette) and neutral control images, with within-participant contrasts of smoking cue > neutral described. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (cluster-level FWE results and voxelwise ROI-corrected results) in the text and gives coordinates; scanner field strength (3.0T), processing software (SPM12, CONN), participant age/sex (male-only) and cue type (nicotine) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) with clear within-subject contrasts (WATCH Food > WATCH Neutral) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. The methods report whole-brain statistical mapping (thresholding, random-effects one-/two-sample t-tests) and include reported coordinates for regressions; scanner field strength (3T), processing software (SPM8), participant age and sex, and cue type are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

This is an fMRI study of cannabis cue reactivity that includes visual (picture) stimuli and reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., cannabis picture > baseline; cannabis picture > flower picture). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-thresholded maps and described in text/tables/figures). Participant age and sex, cue type (cannabis/pictures), MRI field strength (3.0T), and processing software (FSL, AFNI, ANTS) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and does not violate exclusion criteria.

The study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. It uses an individualized guided-imagery (auditory/script) task rather than visual stimuli, so it fails I3. Additionally, the paper reports voxel-wise connectivity (ICD) and seed-based connectivity analyses during task periods but does not report task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts (e.g., food>control) required by the review; thus it falls under exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity-only without a whole-brain task activation map). No qualifying within-participant visual cue>control whole-brain activation maps are provided. Full text appears complete.

This article is a study protocol without reported empirical fMRI results or group-level whole-brain activation maps. It describes a planned cue-reactivity fMRI paradigm using alcoholic beverage images and planned GLM analyses, but no task-evoked, group-level whole-brain statistical maps or coordinates are presented. Therefore it does not provide original, analyzable whole-brain task activation data required for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual pictorial stimuli, reporting within-subject contrasts (smoking-related > neutral) and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results (thresholds and cluster extents) and reported peak coordinates. Methods report participant age/sex (male, mean age), cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM5). Results include whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables as well as regression analyses of cue-evoked activity. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and is complete for screening purposes.

The study is an fMRI investigation of visual smoking cue reactivity and includes within-participant smoking>neutral contrasts and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL/FreeSurfer). However, the manuscript reports analyses based on extracting beta weights from predefined ROIs (left/right NAc and caudate) rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map, nor are whole-brain results (coordinates/figures/tables) reported. Therefore it violates the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI cannabis cue-reactivity study using visual cues, but the paper reports only dynamic functional connectivity and topological/network analyses (DCC-derived connectivity measures) rather than any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps or coordinates for a drug-cue > control contrast. Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or equivalent coordinate reporting) is not met; the study therefore falls under exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity-only analyses without whole-brain task activation). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (drug images tailored to cocaine, alcohol, nicotine). It reports within-participant contrasts of drug cues > neutral cues at first-level and group-level second-level, random-effects, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with cluster correction and tables/coordinates/figures. Methods state MRI field strength (3.0T Siemens Trio) and preprocessing/analysis software (SPM12; AFNI 3dClustSim used). Participant age/sex and cue types are reported. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli in alcohol-dependent patients and controls. It includes within-subject contrasts (alcohol cues > neutral cues) at the single-subject level and group-level analyses. Although primary reported findings are ROI-corrected, the manuscript explicitly reports whole-brain (uncorrected) exploratory activations in the Supplementary material (i.e., group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain results reported in text/tables/supplement. Relevant details (participant age/sex, cue type, 3 T scanner, SPM12 processing) are provided. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity that includes visual smoking cues and directly compares smoking-related versus neutral picture blocks within participants (CIG-I > NEU-I). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster Z>2.3, p<0.05) with detailed results described in text and figures/tables. Necessary study descriptors are provided: participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper is a task-based fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral) at the group level. Whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses are described (flexible factorial, two-sample and paired t tests) with cluster thresholds and small-volume FWE corrections; peak coordinates and cluster results are reported. Participant age/sex information, cue type (alcohol visual cues), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are all provided. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). It does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity, or between-group-only contrasts. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in AUD participants but it does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/food/sexual cues. The tasks used emotional faces (angry/fearful vs. forms) and a dot-probe for attentional bias to emotional expressions, not alcohol-related visual cues. Therefore it does not provide a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast required for inclusion. The study does report whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and provides coordinates and processing details (SPM, AFNI, 3T scanner, age/sex), but it fails key inclusion criteria I3 and I4. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual alcohol-related cues (alcohol pictures) with within-participant contrasts of alcohol-related > neutral pictures. The methods describe voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (voxelwise t-tests, whole-brain corrected thresholds, Talairach coordinates and reported cluster/coordinate results), and seed-based/resting analyses in addition. Relevant metadata are provided: participant numbers and ages, cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (TurboBrainVoyager/BrainVoyager, AFNI, FSL). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain cue-reactivity using visual stimuli are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of drug cue-reactivity that includes a visual cigarette cue paradigm (first-person video cues) and reports within-subject contrasts (Cigarette Cues > Control and Alcohol Cues > Control). Whole-brain GLMs were run (FEAT/FSL), peak precuneus coordinates are reported in MNI space, and group-level voxelwise analyses were performed to define ROIs via a leave-one-out whole-brain approach. Participant age/sex, cue types (nicotine and alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The cigarette cue component uses visual stimuli, satisfying the visual-stimuli requirement. Results (including coordinates) are reported and meet the meta-analysis reporting requirements. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (tobacco) with within-participant contrasts (tobacco vs neutral and tobacco vs money). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (disjunction mask, cluster thresholds, AlphaSim correction) and presents cluster results and coordinates. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type, scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (AFNI) are all reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an empirical fMRI study of food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images). The design includes within-subject contrasts of food vs. matched object control stimuli, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects FLAME in FSL) with permutation-based cluster correction. The paper reports participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3 T Siemens Skyra), and processing software (FSL), satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues (ISIS) to assess cue-reactivity in nicotine-dependent smokers and matched nonsmokers. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (Smoking > neutral) and multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM8) with reported cluster thresholds and MNI coordinates. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although the sample size is small and some analyses are fixed-effects, all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol and non-alcohol beverage cues in participants with AUD and healthy controls. It reports within-subject contrasts of each stimulus versus a mosaic baseline (stimulus>control), first-level contrasts taken to second-level random-effects analyses, and whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics. Key study details required by the review are reported (participant age/sex, cue type = alcohol, scanner field strength = 1.5T, processing software = SPM12). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This study reports resting-state functional connectivity and correlational analyses of salience network coupling and ADHD symptoms in smokers versus non-smokers. It does not include any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual drug or natural reward cues, nor any within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control stimuli. No group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or activation contrasts are reported. Therefore it fails the meta-analysis inclusion criteria requiring task-based visual cue-reactivity fMRI and instead meets exclusion criteria for resting-state/seed-based connectivity-only studies.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, employing within-subject Craving>Neutral contrasts and group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses. The paper reports voxelwise results (coordinates, cluster sizes) and contrasts for Craving>Neutral within groups and for Schizophrenia>Controls, specifies cue type (cigarette/nicotine), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an fMRI study of visual smoking cue-reactivity in nicotine-dependent humans that reports a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast and presents group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation results (cluster reported with MNI coordinates) using FSL Randomise. Participant sex and age information are reported, cue type is nicotine (visual stimuli), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are described. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study used fMRI and visual word stimuli and performed whole-brain voxelwise analyses, but its primary reported contrasts concern monetary reward (50¢>0¢). Although drug-related and neutral words were presented, the authors report no within-subject analyses or whole-brain results contrasting drug cues > control (drug>neutral) and explicitly collapsed across word type. Therefore it does not provide the required within-participant cue-reactivity contrast (I4) needed for inclusion in this meta-analysis of drug/natural reward cue-reactivity. It does report whole-brain maps and participant/scan/process details, but the absence of any drug-cue>control whole-brain task effect prevents inclusion.

This study is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cannabis cues and neutral control stimuli, reporting within-subject contrasts (cannabis cue > neutral) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and voxelwise t tests). Participant characteristics (male-only sample, group sizes, dependence status) and cue type (cannabis) are reported; fMRI acquisition and processing details are indicated in the methods/supplement. Results include whole-brain task-evoked activation maps described in the text and region coordinates, as well as behavioral–neural contrasts. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this paper is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual drug/alcohol cues and reports within-subject drug/alcohol > neutral contrasts (satisfying I3 and I4) and reports participant demographics and acquisition/processing details (I7), its primary reported analyses are seed-based task-modulated functional connectivity (gPPI) across predefined ROIs. The manuscript does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map for the drug>control contrast. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (seed-based/effective connectivity only without whole-brain task maps). Full text appears complete.

This is a resting-state seed-based functional connectivity study comparing smokers and nonsmokers and assessing acute smoking effects. It does not present any task-based cue-reactivity paradigm using visual drug or natural-reward cues, provides no within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control stimuli, and reports no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity fMRI studies and meets exclusion criterion E4 (seed-based/connectivity or resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos). It includes within-participant contrasts (smoking > non-smoking control videos), reports group-level voxelwise statistical maps and t-maps with correction and peak coordinates (tables/figures), and provides required participant and methods details (age, sex, cue type nicotine, 3 T scanner, processing software NIAK/fmristat). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary tables/figures are referenced. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of cocaine and paraphernalia). It reports within-participant cocaine>neutral contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-test and 2×2 mixed-effects ANOVA) with cluster- and voxelwise thresholds, and reports peak coordinates/clusters. Relevant participant information is provided (age range 18–65, men and women, n=25 with final n reported), cue type (cocaine), MRI field strength (Siemens 3.0T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of insula functional connectivity following 12 h smoking abstinence. It does not use a task-based visual cue paradigm nor report any within-participant contrasts of drug cues > control stimuli. All reported analyses are seed-based resting-state connectivity (RSFC) and voxelwise resting-state contrasts (abstinence vs satiety), not task-evoked cue-reactivity maps. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I3 or I4 and falls squarely under exclusion criterion E4 (resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). The full text provided appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of performance feedback in abstinent smokers using a motion-prediction task with emoji feedback, not a cue-reactivity paradigm. It does not present drug-related or natural-reward visual cues (e.g., images of nicotine, alcohol, food, sexual stimuli) nor report any within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control or natural-reward-cue > control. Although the paper includes group-level whole-brain task activation maps and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software, it fails to meet core inclusion criteria I3 and I4 required for a cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Therefore it must be excluded.

Although this is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts and full reporting of participant demographics and scanner/software (meets I3, I4, I7), the primary analyses are ROI-based MVPA in the lateral occipital complex. The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for cigarette>control (or equivalent) contrasts — only a whole-brain localizer for object regions and ROI-based results are presented. Therefore it lacks the required whole-brain task activation map (I5) and must be excluded per E3 (ROI-only results without whole-brain task maps). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) in humans. It includes within-participant contrasts of natural reward cues > control (high-calorie food vs low-calorie food; food vs nonfood) and reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM12) acquired on a 3T scanner. Relevant study/sample information (participant ages, cue type, MRI field strength, processing software) are reported. Results are reported as whole-brain cluster-level findings (text/tables/figures). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for visual natural-reward cue-reactivity fMRI and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not non-empirical).

This is an fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli that reports within-subject heroin-related > neutral cue contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with correction; it provides relevant participant information (male subjects), scanner field strength (3T), cue type (heroin), and processing software. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3–I7) and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study).

Although this is an fMRI study of nicotine cue reactivity (participants exposed to cigarette vs neutral cues) and includes within-subject comparisons, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. Analyses focus on ROI-based activation and directed/effective connectivity (uSEM/GIMME) without accompanying unmasked whole-brain task activation results. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria for studies reporting only ROI/effective connectivity analyses without whole-brain results. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual/video stimuli, includes within-participant contrasts (craving-inducing cues vs mosaic control; aversion-inducing cues vs mosaic), and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results (voxelwise SPMs with FDR thresholds and reported cluster-wise findings). Methods report scanner field strength (1.5T) and processing software (BrainVoyager BVQX 1.9); participant demographics (age and sex) are described in the text as compared between groups and group sizes are given. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Meets all required inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images) with within-subject contrasts (COC > NEU). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses for the COC > NEU contrast (between-group t-tests) and describes within-group activations; it provides participant age/sex, cue type (cocaine), MRI field strength (3.0T) and processing software (BrainVoyager). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

Although this is an fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity in regular users (visual drug cues implied) and reports participant age/sex and scanner field strength, the provided full text does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation results or coordinate tables/figures for the critical within-participant contrast (drug cues > control). Processing/analysis software is not reported in the main text (likely in supplementary material not provided). The main results focus on treatment (between-group) effects and ROIs; no unmasked whole-brain task maps or clear within-subject cue>control contrasts are available in the provided content, so the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis.

This is a human fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes visual stimuli (food pictures). Subject-level contrasts included HFHS vs LFLS, HFHS vs NF, and HFHS vs rest for pictures; group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM12, 3T scanner) reporting cluster results and extracted beta values. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength, and processing software are reported. Although many group tests focus on pre-to-post (surgery) changes, the study computed the requisite within-participant cue>control contrasts and produced whole-brain group-level maps of these contrasts (as pre-post difference maps). Thus the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for fMRI visual natural reward cue-reactivity.

This full-text reports an empirical fMRI study using visual drug cues (cannabis) in cannabis-dependent adults. It includes within-subject contrasts of cannabis cues > Gaussian baseline and cannabis cues > nature/food, using group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses conducted in SPM5 on a 3T scanner, with results reported as clusters/regions and correlations. Participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength, and processing software are all reported. The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity.

This is an fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (cocaine-word Stroop) with a within-subject contrast (Cocaine Words > Neutral Words). The authors performed a voxelwise, group-level SPM12 random-effects whole-brain analysis for the CW minus NW contrast (results reported, including uncorrected cluster-level findings and coordinates used for DCM node selection). Participant demographics (age range, majority male), cue type (cocaine), scanner field strength (Philips 3.0T), and preprocessing/software (AFNI for despiking, SPM12) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not an ROI-only, not connectivity-only without whole-brain activation, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cannabis cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The task included within-participant contrasts of cannabis vs. non-cannabis images and produced voxelwise whole-brain group-level statistical maps (thresholding and cluster-correction reported). The manuscript reports participant age/sex, cue type (cannabis), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Whole-brain analyses were performed in addition to ROI analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues and matched neutral images; it reports within-subject drug cue > neutral contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (paired t-tests and whole-brain correlations) with cluster-corrected results and reported coordinates. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL) are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study comparing neural responses to cannabis cues, natural reward (fruit) cues, and neutral cues in long-term daily cannabis users and non-users. It includes within-participant contrasts (cannabis>neutral; cannabis>fruit; fruit>neutral), and reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FEAT/FLAME) with corrected cluster thresholds. Visual stimuli were used (visual presentations of cannabis paraphernalia and fruit), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM8, FSL/FEAT) are reported. Demographic information is indicated in the methods and referenced tables (participants, exclusion criteria), and cue types and behavioral measures are described. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, meeting core content requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with fasting participants, satisfying the review’s focus on visual cue-reactivity. Within-subject contrasts of food>neutral (scrambled) images were computed and entered into group-level analyses. The paper reports a group-level whole-brain one-sample t-test (FDR-corrected) showing task-evoked activation across limbic and visual regions, meeting the requirement for a voxelwise whole-brain task map; although the primary between-group comparison was ROI-restricted, whole-brain task results are reported and described in the text. Key methodological details are provided (3T scanner, SPM5, cue type = food, sample size and matching for age/sex). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcohol images vs soft drink images) with a within-subject contrast (alcohol blocks > soft drink blocks). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (exploratory whole-brain results with MNI coordinates and cluster-corrected p-values are provided). Relevant methodological details are reported: participant characteristics (all male, groups matched for age), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). The paper also reports ROI results but does not restrict itself to ROI-only analyses. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Accordingly, the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/food/sexual cues. It manipulates monetary reward contingencies during a counting Stroop task in cocaine-dependent and healthy control participants, not presentation of drug or natural reward cues (e.g., cocaine images vs control images). There is no within-participant contrast of drug-cue > control stimuli or natural-reward-cue > control stimuli, so I3 and I4 are not met. Although the paper reports participant demographics, scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM8) (satisfying I7), it does not meet the core cue-reactivity inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking cues with within-subject SC > non-SC contrasts and adequate reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, all voxelwise analyses were conducted within an a priori ROI mask (ROI-restricted voxelwise results) rather than providing an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. The manuscript therefore reports only ROI-restricted results and does not provide whole-brain task activation maps or unmasked whole-brain coordinate tables, which fails the review’s requirement for whole-brain evidence. Per exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain findings), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (e.g., fattening food > object), and reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner (3T) and software (FSL). However, group analyses were conducted using a region-of-interest (ROI) approach only, and the authors explicitly state they “limited our investigation to regions of interest.” No unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level activation map is reported. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures indicating puffs vs money vs neutral). It reports within-subject contrasts (puff>neutral and money>neutral) comparing abstinent and nonabstinent states. Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported (exploratory whole-brain maps at p<.001 with cluster threshold), and key methodological/reporting details are provided (participant ages and sex, cue type: nicotine, scanner field strength 3.0T, processing software SPM8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete for screening. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This study is an fMRI investigation of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of heroin-related images > neutral images, presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (FDR-corrected) with regional coordinates and figures, and provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). Although the paper also includes resting-state/graph-theory analyses, it additionally reports the required whole-brain task activation maps, so no exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue stimuli (water-related and drug-related pictures) in heroin users. It reports within-subject contrasts (Thirst vs Neutral and Drug vs Neutral) at the group level using voxelwise, whole-brain SPM2 second-level one-sample t-tests, and reports peak coordinates and cluster information. Participant age and sex, scanner field strength (1.5T), cue types (heroin, water), and processing software (SPM2) are provided. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusion criteria.

Although this is an fMRI study of a natural reward (juice) with a visual cue and reports sufficient participant and scanning details, the paper's results are reported primarily as a priori ROI analyses. The manuscript does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or an explicit within-participant contrast of reward-predictive visual cues versus neutral/control visual stimuli. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results and a within-participant cue>control analysis required for inclusion. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with within-participant contrasts (food > non-food) and reports key methodological details (age/sex, cue type, 3T scanner, FSL processing), the group-level statistical analysis was conducted using a masked, ROI-based approach (a priori anatomical masks fed to FSL RANDOMISE). The paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study using visual heroin cues with within-subject (heroin > neutral) contrasts and whole-brain, voxelwise SPM8 analyses on a 3.0 T scanner; however, the provided full text does not explicitly report participant sex/gender breakdown (the demographic details appear missing: “demographically matched ( )”), and therefore criterion I7 (relevant information reported regarding participant age and sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and processing software) is not fully satisfied. All other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Because at least one required inclusion criterion is not met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis based on the provided full text.

This is an fMRI study of multisensory numeric Stroop (cognitive control) in recently abstinent cocaine users vs. controls. Although it uses whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports group differences, it does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, nor does it include any within-participant contrasts of drug-cues > control stimuli (or natural reward cues > control). Therefore it fails the review’s primary inclusion criteria (I3 and I4). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) but the experimental task is not a cue-reactivity paradigm. Exclusion is based on lack of cue-reactivity contrasts required for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual reward-predicting cues (money and cigarettes) and an event-related design. The authors performed within-subject contrasts of anticipation to reward-predicting stimuli (parametric increase across reward levels, including 0/no-reward trials) for cigarette and monetary cues, enabling drug-cue>control and natural-reward>control contrasts. Analyses were conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM5 analyses with reported whole-brain results (thresholding described, clusters and peak coordinates referenced), and MRI field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM5) are specified. Participant demographics (age and sex) are reported in the paper’s subject data/tables (referenced in the text). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

The full text reports an fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (color-word drug Stroop) in cocaine-dependent participants, with within-participant drug vs. matched neutral contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects t-tests and voxelwise regression/correlation maps are described and reported (voxelwise results and ROI confirmations), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps even though some drug>neutral contrasts did not reach cluster-corrected significance. Key methodological details are provided (participant ages/sex, cue type: cocaine, scanner field strength: 4T, processing software: SPM2). The article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting) apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cue reactivity to cannabis using visual stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts (cannabis vs. neutral) with coordinate tables and ROI results. However, the reported analyses are ROI-focused with small-volume FWE corrections and Bonferroni correction across a priori ROIs; no unambiguous whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (or whole-brain cluster-corrected results) are presented. Because the paper appears to report only ROI analyses without accompanying whole-brain task maps, it fails the whole-brain reporting requirement and meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an fMRI investigation of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual smoking-related vs neutral images with within-subject contrasts (smoking>neutral). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group peak in mPFC with cluster-corrected p-value) and provides coordinate data and cluster information. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0T Siemens Trio), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is a single-case (n=1) fMRI study reporting pre/post/relapse task activations to alcohol vs non-alcohol images, but it does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical map required by the meta-analysis. The paper reports region activations qualitatively for the single subject and refers to figures/supplement but lacks a group analysis. Additionally, key methodological details required by I7 (MRI scanner field strength and processing software) are not reported in the provided full text. While the study meets I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual alcohol cues) and I4 (within-participant alcohol cues > control contrast), it fails I5 (group-level whole-brain results) and does not fully satisfy I7. Therefore it must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with voxelwise thresholds and AlphaSim-corrected cluster sizes; results are reported as coordinates and figures. Participant age range and sex distribution are provided, scanner field strength (3T Philips Intera) and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues with within-subject contrasts (heroin-related vs. neutral) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects, paired t-tests). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported. Results include whole-brain activations presented in text/tables/coordinates. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of practice/habituation effects on a sustained attention task with monetary incentives, not a visual cue-reactivity study. It does not present any within-participant contrasts comparing drug-related or natural reward-related visual cues versus control stimuli (no drug-cue > control or food/sexual cue contrasts). Although whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses are reported (and participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software are described), the key eligibility for this meta-analysis (I3/I4) is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis of visual drug/natural reward cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food). It includes within-subject contrasts of hedonic food cues > nonfood control stimuli, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and MNI coordinates. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visually presented drug-related words (visual stimuli). The paper reports within-participant cocaine>neutral (drug cues vs control stimuli) contrasts and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group contrast maps with FWE correction). Relevant metadata are provided (participant age/sex reporting, cocaine cue type, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software CamBA/SPM). The study therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual stimuli (pictures) of gambling (natural reward) and smoking (drug) cues, with within-subject contrasts (gambling>neutral; smoking>neutral). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM2; cluster-level correction; coordinates and figures/tables provided). Relevant methodological details are reported (all-male sample, cue types, 3.0T scanner, SPM2 processing). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual cocaine-related stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (Cocaine > Neutral) at the first level and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain analyses and voxel coordinates are reported (including exploratory whole-brain results and specific MNI coordinates for group effects), and ROI analyses are complemented by small-volume corrections; processing details (SPM8) and MR field strength (3.0 T) are provided. Participant information and demographics are described (groups matched on age and sex), and cue type is cocaine.
