This is an fMRI study using visual food cues and within-subject contrasts of high-calorie versus low-calorie foods, and reports participant details; however, the reported analyses are ROI-based (parameter estimates extracted from a priori ROIs) with no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or coordinate tables presented in the full text. Inclusion requires at least one whole-brain, group-level task activation map (voxelwise) or clearly described whole-brain results. Therefore the study must be excluded (E3).

This study investigates maternal neural responses to infant faces and cries (social/parental cues), not drug cues or the natural reward types targeted in the review (e.g., food or sexual cues). It therefore does not satisfy key inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli of the specified types) or I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli). The full text is complete and does report whole-brain voxelwise analyses (satisfying I5), reports whole-brain results in the text/tables (I6), and provides participant/scanner/processing details (I7). Because I3 and I4 are not met, the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study of food (natural reward) cues meets multiple inclusion criteria: it uses visual food stimuli (I3), reports within-participant contrasts (highly desirable>less desirable; food>non-food) (I4), and reports group-level second-level voxelwise statistics with coordinate-level results and SVC-corrected peaks (I5,I6). However, it does not report essential participant age information or explicitly state the primary processing software used (only indirect mention of marsbar), so it fails inclusion criterion I7 requiring relevant info on participant age, sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an fMRI investigation of food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-participant contrasts (fattening food > object, non-fattening > object). It reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). However, group-level analyses were conducted using a region-of-interest (14 predefined ROIs) approach with cluster-thresholding within ROIs; the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group task-evoked statistical map. Because the study reports only ROI-based group analyses and no whole-brain group activation map, it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of sexual (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual pornographic stimuli with within-subject pornographic>neutral contrasts and group-level whole-brain analyses (SPM12). Participant age and sex are reported. However, the manuscript does not report MRI scanner field strength (fMRI acquisition section refers to another source: 'See .'), so it fails inclusion criterion I7 requiring relevant reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. All other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met. Because I7 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded per the review rules (any unmet inclusion criterion leads to exclusion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (food vs. non-food and food vs. blurry baseline) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (t-tests and ANOVA) with cluster-corrected thresholds; coordinates and Talairach/BA locations are provided for key effects. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual monetary incentive cues (rings of $ vs #) and reports within-subject contrasts of reward>neutral (natural reward-related cues vs control). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were performed (AFNI 3dLME) with cluster-level correction and reported statistical maps/ROIs. Participant age and sex, cue type (monetary), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (FSL, AFNI) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-subject task effects).

Although this is an fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (food) with clearly reported participants, scanner (3T), stimuli, and SPM2 processing, the analyses are reported using an a priori ROI approach with small-volume correction within defined ROIs. The paper does not present unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps; results are confined to ROIs and SVC-corrected clusters. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual nicotine cues and within-subject task conditions (smoke, neutral, rest), the provided full text reports individualized ROI selection and ROI-based neurofeedback analyses (percent signal change within subject-tailored vACC/dmPFC ROIs) and group-level t-tests on these ROIs. The manuscript does not present or describe an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinate table of whole-brain smoke>neutral activation. Therefore it reports only ROI-based results without qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results, meeting exclusion criterion E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with event-related presentation of food vs visually matched non-food images. The paper reports within-participant contrasts of food>non-food, whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (FEAT/FSL) with cluster correction and tables/figures of activations, and provides participant age range/sex information, cue type (food), scanner field strength (Philips 3T), and processing software (FSL). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual cues with within-subject contrasts (HC–control, LC–control) and adequate reporting of participants, scanner (3T), and processing (SPM8), the reported analyses and results are presented as ROI-based/small-volume-corrected activations rather than unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps. The manuscript describes a second-level repeated measures ANOVA but applies an a priori ROI analysis (masks and small-volume correction) and reports ROI activations; there is no clear presentation of unmasked whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain corrected results. Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only results) and does not satisfy the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task activation map (I5). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that presented visual food stimuli (also auditory) and analyzed within-subject contrasts (high- vs low-calorie foods and food vs non-food). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8 with cluster-correction and reported task-evoked statistical maps/clusters (with thresholds and cluster extent determined by AlphaSim), satisfying whole-brain reporting standards. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of natural (sexual/social) reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (male/female faces). It reports within-participant contrasts related to reward cues versus control stimuli (anticipation of smiling faces vs dysmorphed control images) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain results for main effects and exploratory whole-brain results with coordinates). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (sexual/face stimuli), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of smoking cue reactivity using audio/visual (visual) stimuli and includes within-participant contrasts of smoking cues versus matched non-smoking cues. However, all reported group-level analyses were conducted within an a priori ROI mask (ventral medial PFC, ventral striatum/pallidum, insula, hippocampus, amygdala, and dorsal striatum added retrospectively). The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map at the group level; results are limited to ROI-based inference. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. The study reports within-participant contrasts of food>object (food vs. matched object images) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected permutation tests) as well as ROI analyses. Relevant details are provided: participant age and sex, cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (FSL). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for visual-cue reward fMRI studies.

This study reports development and behavioral validation of visual cue pictures and an fMRI paradigm but did not acquire or analyze any fMRI data. It reports self-reported VAS craving only and no within-participant fMRI contrast of drug-cue > control, no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate results. Therefore it does not meet the core inclusion requirements for neuroimaging studies (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). It is a methods/behavioral validation paper without original human fMRI results, so it must be excluded from a meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs. non-alcohol beverage pictures) in adolescents. It reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol>non-alcohol) and conducts both ROI and exploratory whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (3dttest++ with cluster correction), with results described in the text for whole-brain clusters. The paper provides participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue reactivity using visual smoking images and within-subject smoking>nonsmoking contrasts, and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, all reported task analyses focus on ROI-based parameter estimates and targeted ROI/mediation models; the manuscript does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or whole-brain coordinates/figures of an unmasked task effect. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an fMRI investigation of natural reward (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli, with a within-subject food > nonfood contrast and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported. The manuscript provides participant demographics (age, sex distribution implied), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). Whole-brain statistical maps (F, t, r) and cluster-level correction procedures are described; results are reported across the brain and referenced to anatomical labels, fulfilling acceptable reporting via text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are violated.

This is an empirical 3T fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts comparing food pictures versus neutral objects. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (RFX ANOVA F-maps and conjunction t-maps) are reported, with thresholding and Talairach coordinates for identified fROIs. Relevant participant information (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for visual natural reward cue-reactivity fMRI studies are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and reports participant demographics and scanner/processing details (meets I3 and I7). However, it does not report a within-participant contrast of reward cues > control (no food>neutral or food>non-food contrast); instead contrasts Enhance vs Regulate (both conditions use palatable food images), so I4 is not met. Additionally, group analyses were performed using ROI-based small-volume correction without reporting unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps; thus the study effectively reports only ROI-corrected results, triggering exclusion under E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts of food > scenery. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (t maps, peak coordinates, cluster thresholds), and results are described in text, tables, and figures. Participant age/sex (healthy adult males), cue type (food), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software (fmristat) are provided. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of food cue reactivity using personalized guided-imagery (auditory) scripts rather than visual stimuli. The review’s I3 requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, which is not met. The study does meet several other inclusion criteria (within-subject contrasts of favorite-food cue > neutral, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected maps and coordinates reported, and relevant participant/cue/scanner information), but failure to use visual cues is sufficient to exclude it from this meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cost–benefit decision making using a Cigarette Purchase Task (economic choices about purchasing cigarettes), not a cue-reactivity paradigm presenting visual drug- or reward-related cues. It does not include within-participant contrasts of drug-cue > control-stimuli or natural-reward-cue > control-stimuli. The paper does report group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and provides participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength and processing software, so it meets I5, I6, and I7, but it fails to meet key inclusion criteria I3 and I4. Therefore it must be excluded from this meta-analysis focused on visual cue-reactivity.

The article does not report task-based fMRI cue-reactivity using visual drug or natural-reward cues. The neuroimaging reported is resting-state fMRI and diffusion tensor imaging (structural) in relation to mindfulness training; behavioral measures (craving, smoking) are reported but there are no within-subject contrasts of drug-cue > control-stimuli or whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Thus it fails to meet inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5 and matches exclusion criterion E4 (resting-state/structural analyses without a whole-brain task activation map).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related cue-reactivity (food) using visual stimuli (food words). It includes within-subject contrasts of food>neutral (food-fneu) at the group level, reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and statistical thresholds, and provides participant demographics (age, sex distribution), cue type (food words), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Results are reported as whole-brain effects and coordinates in the text/tables, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues and a within-participant contrast (alcohol > pleasant). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (activation in left caudate and occipital cortex) with coordinates and cluster sizes described in the text and refers to supplemental materials for full acquisition and preprocessing details. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is alcohol, and scanner/acquisition/processing details are indicated to be available in the Supplement. The study therefore satisfies the review’s requirements for an fMRI drug-cue visual stimulus task, a within-subject drug>control contrast, whole-brain results reported in the text/tables, and reporting of participant and methodological details (with additional scanner/software details provided in supplement). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains whole-brain within-subject effects, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food pictures) with within-participant contrasts of food vs non-food stimuli, and group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (random-effects, voxelwise maps) identifying brain regions responsive to food cues. Participant age and sex and cue type are reported; MRI acquisition and preprocessing details are indicated to be provided in the supplementary material, satisfying reporting requirements. The study thus meets the meta-analysis objective (visual reward cue-reactivity) and all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task activation maps, is empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of a natural reward (food) using visual cues (milkshake image vs water) and tastes. It reports within-participant contrasts of milkshake cues > control (milkshake picture > water picture) and milkshake taste > tasteless, and conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using FSL with cluster-based correction. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are all reported. Results are presented as whole-brain clusters described in the text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject contrast of high-calorie > low-calorie food images. The methods report fMRI acquisition (3T) and processing (SPM8) and participant age/sex characteristics. Although the primary reported effect is in the hypothalamus using an ROI and small-volume correction, the authors explicitly state they carried out an exploratory whole-brain (voxelwise) analysis (at p<0.05 FWE) and report the outcome (no other regional differences). Thus a group-level whole-brain task analysis was performed and reported in the text. All required information (cue type, scanner field strength, software) is provided and the full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Given these elements, the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual natural reward cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) and reports within-participant contrasts relevant to cue-reactivity (e.g., healthy-food-choice > healthy-food-reject, and Tasty-Diet (TD) > No-Diet (ND) conditions), conducted at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8). Coordinates and cluster results are reported and scanner parameters (3T), participant age/sex/BMI, cue type (food), and processing software are provided. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual natural reward cue-reactivity with whole-brain results.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (a natural reward). It contains within-subject contrasts of food > nonfood, reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with corrected cluster results and coordinates, and provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) with a within-participant contrast of palatable food > neutral items. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (FWE-corrected effects, Talairach/MNI coordinates reported), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The paper reports participant age range (adolescents/young adults), mentions sex comparisons, cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3.0T) and processing software (SPM8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward-related (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject contrasts of high-calorie vs. non-food images (pre- and post-meal), and presents group-level whole-brain, voxelwise statistical maps with cluster-based correction and Talairach coordinates. Relevant metadata are provided (participant age and sex, cue type = food, scanner field strength = 3.0 T, processing software = BrainVoyager). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (food pictures) vs nonfood control (animals) to assess reward-related cue reactivity in overweight adolescent girls. The study reports within-participant contrasts (food > nonfood) and conducts group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses with cluster-level correction. Key methodological details required by the review are reported: participant age and sex (15–20 y, female), cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3-Tesla Siemens Trio), and processing software (Brain Voyager QX). Full article text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI investigation of response inhibition using abstract visual stimuli (geometric shapes) in methamphetamine-dependent and control participants. It does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity (no drug/food/sexual cues), nor does it include a within-subject contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural-reward cues > control stimuli. Thus it fails inclusion criteria I3 and I4. The full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, and discussion).

This is a human fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of cocaine/paraphernalia). It includes a within-subject contrast of cocaine pictures > neutral objects and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses using SPM8 with cluster-level correction, with results described in the text (activation in putamen, insula, occipital cortex) and supplemental figures. Relevant participant information (age range 18–65, men and women), cue type (cocaine), MRI field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an adult fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts of alcohol vs. neutral cues. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample t-test of alcohol>neutral, whole-brain regression vs. SCR) with peak coordinates and cluster statistics described. Participant demographics (age used as covariate, sex counts reported), cue type (alcohol), and processing software (SPM) are specified; scanner details are likely in the Supplement (acceptable per inclusion criteria). The study therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements for visual cue fMRI whole-brain task activation maps and reports necessary methodological details.

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (beer images) in a Go/NoGo task comparing responses to alcohol vs non-alcohol stimuli. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (thresholded whole-brain maps) and presents activation maps for NoGo (beer) trials and between-group contrasts (heavy > light) with whole-brain inference. Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. Individual subject-level contrasts for Go and NoGo conditions were created and entered into second-level analyses, providing the within-participant condition contrasts needed for cue>control comparisons. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues with within-participant food>non-food contrasts and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, the manuscript reports results derived from region-of-interest (ROI) percent signal-change extractions and does not present or describe group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, coordinates, or cluster tables in the provided full text. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results).

Although this is an empirical fMRI study in cocaine-dependent individuals that includes cue exposure for behavioral craving measures, the MRI analyses do not report a within-participant visual cue-reactivity contrast (drug cues > control stimuli). The reported whole-brain voxelwise maps are TMS-evoked BOLD responses and pre/post cTBS (real vs sham) effects, not task-based cue-reactivity to visual drug cues. Therefore criteria I3 and I4 (fMRI of visual cue-reactivity and a within-subject cue>control contrast) are not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present) but no qualifying cue-reactivity fMRI maps are described. Exclusion from the meta-analysis is warranted.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts (viewing food > viewing non-food; distraction food > distraction non-food). Analyses are group-level whole-brain voxelwise using SPM8 with reported cluster coordinates and thresholding (FWE cluster-corrected), and the paper reports participant sex/age, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (sexual) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures/videos and written visual cues). It includes within-subject contrasts CUE SEM > CUE NEUTRAL and SEM > NEUTRAL, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected clusters and coordinates), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of monetary reward anticipation using the Monetary Incentive Delay task (visual cues for £5, £1, £0). Although it includes within-participant reward>neutral contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates, and reports participant demographics, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM8), it does not assess drug-related cues or natural reward-related cues (e.g., food, sexual) as defined by the review objective. Monetary reward cues do not meet the meta-analysis’s specified domain of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I3.

This is an empirical fMRI study employing visual alcohol cues (alcohol-related images) and neutral images in an alcohol cue reactivity (ACR) task. It reports within-subject alcohol>neutral contrasts (GLM, one-sample t-tests) and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation results (alcohol > neutral) with voxelwise and cluster-level correction. Participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio) and detailed acquisition parameters are reported; preprocessing is referenced and reported in Supplementary Methods (fulfilling reporting requirements). The study therefore satisfies all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cue-induced desire for Internet video game play using visual stimuli. It includes a within-subject contrast (video-game cue > neutral control), reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects results with coordinates and cluster statistics (FDR-corrected), and provides participant age/sex information, scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). Although the cue type is Internet video game (a behavioral/non-drug reward), the review objective includes drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity; gaming can be considered a non-drug reward cue within that scope. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the inclusion criteria for whole-brain task-evoked cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

The reported fMRI results in this full text focus on emotional face processing (faces vs shapes) and oxytocin modulation, not on drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity contrasts. Although an alcohol cue-reactivity task was performed, its results are reported in a parent study and are not presented here. Therefore the paper does not provide a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast nor a whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map of drug or natural reward cue-reactivity required for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts (smoking > control). However, the voxelwise second-level analyses were conducted within anatomically defined ROI masks (Harvard-Oxford atlases) and results are presented as ROI-based activations/deactivations. There is no evidence in the full text that an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map was performed or reported. Therefore the study reports only ROI-restricted task results and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). The full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in heavy drinkers using visual cues (images) of alcohol and food (natural reward). The AFID task included within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs neutral and alcohol vs food) and the manuscript reports group-level, voxel-wise whole-brain analyses (linear mixed-effects voxel-wise analyses across the entire brain) with thresholding and cluster correction. Relevant methodological details are reported (participant age/sex information, cue types: alcohol and food, MRI scanner field strength 3T, and processing software AFNI). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided content appears complete for screening. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original human fMRI study that uses visual natural reward cues (high-calorie food images) and includes within-participant contrasts of food>control (food vs low-level baseline and food vs non-food). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (group activation maps, between-group whole-brain comparisons with Talairach coordinates and cluster results). Reporting includes participant sex (female), demographic comparisons, cue type (food), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software (XBAM v4.1). The full text (background, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a human fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (erotic and monetary images) with within-subject contrasts. The task includes outcome trials (viewing erotic pictures) versus missed (scrambled) trials and contrasts of high>low erotic cues; analyses used subject-level models and second-level random-effects paired t-tests. Results are reported with voxelwise statistics in figures and coordinate-based ROI peak values, and full methods report scanner field strength (3T) and SPM12 processing, as well as participant age and sex. Thus it meets: I3 (fMRI with visual natural rewards: sexual), I4 (within-participant contrasts of reward-related cues vs control/missed trials and high>low cue contrasts), I5 (group-level second-level random effects maps were generated), I6 (coordinates/figures reported), and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, scanner, software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper includes an original empirical fMRI dataset examining neural responses to visual food cues (natural reward) in children (7–11 years). It reports within-participant contrasts of high-ED vs low-ED food images, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI) with multiple-comparisons correction, and reports peak coordinates and cluster sizes. Participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI) are all reported. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation using visual natural-reward cues (food images) with an explicit within-participant contrast of food > nonfood stimuli. It reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected Monte Carlo simulations) and also ROI analyses, with whole-brain results described in text and reported by coordinates. Participant demographics (sex, age range), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager 20.6) are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (the study does not report only ROI/connectivity/between-group-only results and is not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (meets I3) and reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps (respond alcohol > rest and respond neutral > rest) with cluster correction (meets I5 and I6) and provides participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (meets I7), the study does NOT present a within-participant contrast of alcohol cues > control stimuli (respond alcohol versus respond neutral). The authors explicitly state that direct comparisons of the two response conditions were not conducted because the task design did not allow a clean contrast. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met, and the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of visual natural reward cues (high-calorie and low-calorie food images) in adolescents. It includes within-participant contrasts (HCF>NF and LCF>NF), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction (supplementary tables/figures and described in text), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (BioImageSuite, AFNI). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of marzipan objects). It reports within-subject contrasts (CS+ > CS-) at the group level and performed whole-brain voxelwise analysis (one-sample t-test on subject contrasts; whole-brain threshold p<.001 uncorrected with reported clusters), with additional SVC results. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, empirical fMRI task activation map provided). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI investigation of monetary reward anticipation (Monetary Incentive Delay task) rather than drug-related or natural reward (e.g., food, sexual) cue-reactivity. Inclusion criteria I5, I6, and I7 are met: the paper reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, presents whole-brain results/figures, and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). However, it fails I3 and I4 because the cues are monetary (not drug or natural reward cues) and therefore do not provide a within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward cues>control as required by the review objective. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not address the review’s target cue types and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-participant contrasts such as social alcohol > social soda (SA>SS), non-social alcohol > non-social soda (NA>NS), the interaction ((SA>SS)-(NA>NS)), and main effects (alcohol vs soda), meeting the requirement for drug-cues > control contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and thresholded (voxel p<.001, cluster-level FWE p<.05); unthresholded T-maps are available on NeuroVault, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The article provides participant age and sex (male, 18–25), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T PRISMA), and processing software (SPM8, FSL ICA-AROMA). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes task activation maps, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-participant contrasts comparing food (HC and LC) versus neutral pictures, and presents group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (2×3 ANOVA, whole-brain FWE-corrected contrasts) with whole-brain contrast maps described in the text. Participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM5, AFNI, BioImageSuite) are all reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study is a resting-state fMRI study of food ingestion and label expectancy; it does not present a task-based visual cue-reactivity paradigm. Exclusion criterion E4 applies because the reported analyses are resting-state (ALFF, seed-based FC) and not whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for cue>control contrasts. Inclusion criterion I7 is satisfied (participant age/sex, cue type: food, scanner field strength: 3T, processing software: SPM8/DPARSF reported). Inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI study assessing cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), and I6 (qualifying whole-brain task results as described) are not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED.

The study uses an alcohol taste-cue paradigm (gustatory delivery) with brief visual word labels preceding taste, but the primary cue contrast is Alcohol taste > Water taste rather than a visual cue-reactivity contrast. Inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI study assessing cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) is not met. The study does satisfy within-subject Alcohol>Water contrast (I4), reports group-level whole-brain analyses/activation clusters and supplementary materials (I5,I6), and provides participant and methods details including image acquisition in supplements (I7). No exclusion criteria (e.g., E3 ROI-only) apply. Therefore excluded for failing I3.

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures) in 23 cocaine-dependent participants. It reports within-subject contrasts (cocaine > neutral), presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (SPM8; voxelwise FWE-corrected results, tables and figures), and provides participant sex information, scanner field strength (3T), cue type (cocaine), and preprocessing/software details. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This paper is a narrative synthesis/review summarizing a series of ERP and fMRI studies rather than reporting original human fMRI task activation results. Exclusion met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original human fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not present an original fMRI study assessing cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug>control or reward>control contrasts from original data reported), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps presented for new data), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported for original data), I7 (no primary-study participant/sample, scanner field strength, and processing software details for an original fMRI analysis). Full text appears to be a complete review article (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-cue videotapes (cocaine) and reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses. The paper includes within-subject contrasts of cocaine-cue periods versus baseline and versus other emotional (happy/sad) cues, and reports statistical maps (t-maps with voxelwise randomization) and figures/tables of activations. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (cocaine), MRI scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM96) are reported. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains task activation maps, empirical human fMRI data). Accordingly, the study meets all listed inclusion criteria and should be included.

This fMRI study of alcohol cue-induced craving meets several inclusion criteria for the review: I3 (fMRI study using visual alcohol cues), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps were reported for regulation contrasts), I6 (whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables), and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, scanner details, and processing software are reported). However, it does not meet I4: the paper does not present a within-participant, group-level contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (e.g., alcohol > neutral/food) as a primary whole-brain cue-reactivity contrast. The primary reported whole-brain contrasts assess cognitive regulation (LATER>NOW; REAPPRAISE>LOOK) and parametric modulation by craving—not a direct alcohol-cue vs. control stimulus contrast at the group whole-brain level. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded because I4 is not satisfied.

This is an fMRI study using visual drug-related (heroin) cues vs neutral images with within-subject contrasts (BOLD drug-cues > neutral) in heroin-maintained patients. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample and second-level GLMs) and describes whole-brain activation results (clusters and significance thresholds), and additionally provides ROI/OFC analyses. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (heroin), scanner (3T Siemens Magnetom Verio) and processing software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This article reports an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) in pre-pubertal children. It includes a within-subject contrast of food>non-food, and reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<.05) with coordinates and figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-subject Smoking > Neutral contrasts, and performs group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses using FSL/FLAME with cluster correction (results reported in Table 2 and figures). Participant demographics (age range 18–55, gender matching) and cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (FSL) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is noted but not required. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes unmasked whole-brain task effects). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images of cocaine and related objects). It reports within-participant cocaine>neutral contrasts, and conducts group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses using SPM8 with cluster-level thresholding; whole-brain results are reported in tables and figures. Relevant participant information (sex distribution, sample size), cue type (cocaine), MRI field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. The study reports within-subject contrasts (Alcohol > Control) at the first level and conducts group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (second-level GLMs) with cluster-FWE correction; MNI coordinates and cluster details are reported in text/tables/figures. Relevant participant information (age range, sex distribution), cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM12) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task activation, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue modality is gustatory (taste: alcoholic beverage vs juice), not visual stimuli required by the review. Met inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant alcohol>control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with spatial maps/coordinates reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/figures/tables), and I7 (participant sex, cue type, scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (SPM5) reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This paper includes an fMRI experiment in human participants using visual alcohol cues versus neutral pictures and reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol>neutral) and comparisons between intranasal oxytocin and placebo. The fMRI results are reported as whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked effects (Figure 5 and Table 1; significant clusters reported at p<0.05 FWE-corrected), and the manuscript provides participant age and sex and cue type. Scanner and processing details are indicated to be provided in the Supplementary Information (methods and statistics described in detail), which is acceptable per protocol. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied: I3 (fMRI with visual drug cues), I4 (within-participant drug-cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/tabled), and I7 (participant age/sex and cue type reported, scanner/processing details referenced in Supplement). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary materials exist but their absence does not preclude inclusion. Supplementary materials may contain additional methodological details.

The study does not assess visual drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity in the fMRI task. Instead, the fMRI paradigm is a monetary incentive delay task (monetary reward anticipation vs verbal feedback). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control). It does report group-level whole-brain task activation maps and coordinates (satisfies I5 and I6) and provides participant demographics, scanner field strength, and processing software (satisfies I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue videos (cocaine and gambling) to elicit craving/urges. The authors report within-subject contrasts for each video type versus baseline (V1>B1, V2>B2), including drug-cue (cocaine) contrasts versus baseline and versus other videos. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (3×2×3 ANOVAs) with family-wise-error correction and peak coordinates/tables/figures reported. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue types, MRI field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software (SPM5, AFNI) are all provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports whole-brain task activations). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI visual cue-reactivity.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol vs neutral pictures, with within-subject contrasts (alcohol > neutral) at first level and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, two-sample t-tests, and a 2×2 factorial model) reported. Methods report scanner field strength (3 T), preprocessing and analysis software (SPM8/SPM12), participant age range and sex (male only), and cue type (alcohol). Results include whole-brain interaction and main-effect maps, tables, ROI follow-ups, and survival analyses relating neural cue reactivity to relapse. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E3 — the study reports ROI-based PET analyses and does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 — the study includes a within-participant contrast of drug cues > neutral/control cues. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 — this is a PET study measuring dopamine release, not a functional MRI (fMRI) study; I5 — no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported; I6 — no whole-brain results (coordinates/figures) are provided that would satisfy acceptable whole-brain reporting; I7 — required fMRI-specific reporting items (MRI scanner field strength and fMRI processing software) are not provided. Therefore the study does not meet the fMRI-based inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This full-text reports an empirical fMRI study using visual marketing clips of alcohol and cannabis vs neutral clips, with within-subject contrasts (alcohol marketing > neutral; cannabis marketing > neutral). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are described and reported (GLM1 and GLM2; cluster-level FWE results, figures and supporting tables referenced). Participant age/sex, cue types (alcohol, cannabis), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. The manuscript includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. All inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with within-participant contrasts (smoke > rest) and reports participant age/sex, scanner (3T) and processing software (SPM8). However, the report presents only ROI-based analyses (individualized ACC/mPFC ROIs, percent signal change measures and ROI center maps) and does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain activation tables/figures described in the text. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This JoVE protocol reports an fMRI neurofeedback study using visual nicotine cues (meets I3). However, all reported neuroimaging analyses are ROI-based (percent BOLD change from bilateral insula ROIs) and no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, coordinate tables, or figures of whole-brain cue>control contrasts are provided. Participant age/sex are not reported in the full text. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results) and does not meet inclusion criteria I4 (within-participant drug cues > control fMRI contrast reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), or I7 (participant age/sex reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using visual anticipatory cues (MID task) signaling monetary reward/loss (natural reward-related cues). It includes within-subject contrasts (Reward Cue–Neutral Cue and Loss Cue–Neutral Cue), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME whole-brain results with corrected clusters), and provides necessary metadata (participant age/sex, cue type = monetary, 3T scanner field strength, processing software FSL). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study examines alcohol cue-reactivity using visual alcohol pictures (I3 satisfied) and reports within-subject contrasts of alcoholic vs. non-alcoholic beverages (I4 satisfied). It reports coordinates/tables and supplementary materials (I6 satisfied) and provides participant demographics, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) (I7 satisfied). However, the reported second-level voxelwise analyses were spatially restricted to an anatomically-defined mesocorticolimbic mask rather than an unmasked whole-brain group-level voxelwise map, so it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I5 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity that includes visual stimulus conditions (grayscale images of smoking paraphernalia) and reports within-participant contrasts of smoking vs control objects (e.g., VS–VC). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLMs/ANOVAs with cluster-corrected voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: cues were delivered as individualized audiotaped guided-imagery scripts (auditory/imagery), not visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrast: favorite-food vs neutral), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction), I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported in text/tables/figures), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete and sufficient for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli in treatment-seeking smokers. It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > neutral stimuli (CUE>neutral) from a within-subject abstinence vs. satiety design, and conducts group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (paired t-tests) with corrected results (ACC reported). Whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures. Participant age and sex are reported; cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Prisma), and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are provided. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcohol images) and control images during task performance, presenting within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol versus control pictures (e.g., CRAlcohol - CRControl and GOAlcohol - GOControl). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected results, tables of coordinates, and figures). Participant age and sex are reported (ages 21–53, n=53, 29 women), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3.0T Siemens Trio), and processing software (SPM8) are specified. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject contrasts, and is empirical human fMRI data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing tasty food cues to control stimuli (e.g., ADMIT_TASTY>ADMIT_NOT_TASTY) and contrasts of regulation versus craving (REGULATE_TASTY>ADMIT_TASTY). Second-level, group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (voxelwise threshold P<0.001 with cluster-level FWE correction) and results are presented in tables/figures. Relevant participant and methodological details are reported (sample of 43 females; age reported in Table 1; 3 T Siemens scanner; preprocessing and analysis using SPM8/Matlab). The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, refs) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of visual natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that meets all inclusion criteria: it used visual food images, conducted within-subject contrasts (food > nonfood), and reported group-level whole-brain task activation results with voxelwise statistics and coordinates (MNI) and figures. Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (food), 3T MRI, and processing software (SPM12). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical human fMRI data).

Excluded because the fMRI analyses are reported as ROI-based (single-slice vermis ROIs and ROI-derived percent signal change/spatial extent) with no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or group-level whole-brain coordinate table reported (meets Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (empirical fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using audiovisual cocaine cues) and I4 (within-participant contrast of cocaine cues > neutral/control). Inclusion criteria not satisfied: I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map shown), I6 (no group-level whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures/tables for a group map), and I7 (processing software not clearly reported as AFNI/FSL/SPM). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude per review criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue modality is gustatory (alcohol taste cues) rather than visual stimuli required by the meta-analysis. It does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-subject alcohol>water contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software are reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete and includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual stimuli (films) of cocaine, sex, and nature to elicit cue-reactivity in experienced cocaine users and comparison subjects. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (cocaine film vs nature film, sex film comparisons) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample and two-sample t tests thresholded voxel-wise with cluster criteria). Participant age and sex distributions, cue types (cocaine, sexual, nature), MRI scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (AFNI) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues in heavy-drinking participants. It includes within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > rest (cue-reactivity), reports group-level whole-brain (second-level random-effects) statistical analyses (e.g., whole-brain FWE-corrected reward-paradigm activation and whole-brain results for feedback-related activations), and provides necessary methodological/demographic details (participant age/sex, cue type: alcohol, 3T scanner, SPM8 and Turbo-BrainVoyager processing). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual drug cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

Full text appears incomplete and the available content reports only seed-based psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity results; the simple within-subject contrast (alcohol vs neutral) was reported as not significantly different. This means no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map is presented. Exclusion E4 applies (only seed-based connectivity reported without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met based on available text: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity with visual alcohol cues) and I4 (within-participant alcohol>neutral contrast was performed). Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported), I7 (insufficient reporting in the provided extract regarding participant age/sex, scanner field strength, and processing software). Because the full article content is not accessible here, fulltext_incomplete is set to true.

Full text unavailable (page failed to load). Only title/metadata available, which indicate a pharmacological trial measuring craving and withdrawal, not an fMRI cue-reactivity study. Cannot confirm any required fMRI-related methods or whole-brain results. Inclusion criteria not satisfied: I3 (no evidence it is an fMRI study using visual cue-reactivity), I4 (no evidence of within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (no evidence of group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I6 (cannot verify reporting of whole-brain results), I7 (insufficient reporting of MRI parameters or cue details). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 are positively met based on available information. Full text incomplete, so exclusion due to inability to verify inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using audiovisual (visual) stimuli with within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > nonsmoking cues), performed with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) and reporting stereotactic coordinates/tables. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (drug cue fMRI with visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant drug cue>control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses), I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 — the provided full-text does not report MRI scanner field strength (while it does mention processing software SPM5 and demographics are referenced in Table 1, scanner field strength is not present in the provided content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because I7 is not satisfied based on the provided text.

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual videotape stimuli with within-subject contrasts (cue vs baseline) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates. Participant age/sex, cue type (cocaine), and scanner field strength (1.5 T GE Signa) are reported. However, the manuscript does not explicitly report the image processing software/package used (e.g., SPM, FSL, AFNI) as required by inclusion criterion I7. Because I7 is not satisfied, the study cannot be included despite meeting I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports ROI-based cue-reactivity analyses and an additional ROI-constrained voxelwise cluster (left putamen) rather than an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual cannabis stimuli), I4 (within-participant contrast cannabis > neutral/control stimuli), I7 (reported participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [FSL]). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no evidence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the cannabis>control contrast). I6 (reporting of whole-brain results via coordinates/figures) does not apply because the provided coordinates derive from ROI-limited analyses. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to provide whole-brain task activation results required by the meta-analysis.

Full text appears to be limited to abstract-level information. The study is an fMRI investigation using visual food cues (I3 met). However, the provided content does not report whether any within-participant cue>control contrasts were conducted (I4 not confirmed), nor does it state that group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps or coordinate tables/figures are reported (I5/I6 not confirmed). Required methodological details (scanner field strength and processing software) and participant age (beyond ‘adult’) are not reported here (I7 not met). Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be verified, the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis at this time. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on the available information.

This is an fMRI study of monetary reward/loss processing using a monetary incentive delay (MID) task, not a cue-reactivity study presenting drug-related or natural reward (e.g., food/sexual) visual cues. Therefore it does not meet I3 (drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) or I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues>control or natural reward-related cues>control). The study does include whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (I5), reports whole-brain results in text/figures/tables (I6), and provides participant details and processing software (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based task activation analyses and explicitly states that a voxelwise/whole-brain approach was not completed. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual cannabis cues) and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clear within-participant drug-cue > control contrast reported; analyses compare activation during cannabis and neutral pictures but do not present an explicit within-subject contrast of cues>control) and I5 (no group-level whole-brain/voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not satisfy the required whole-brain analysis criterion for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study assesses alcohol (and smoking) cue-reactivity using visual cues in young adults (meets I3), and reports within-participant contrasts of drinking cues > neutral cues (meets I4). It also reports participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM12) (meets I7). However, the paper reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (10 mm spheres in VS and MPFC) with extracted ROI statistics and does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, nor tables/coordinates or whole-brain figures to qualify as whole-brain results. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results) and fails to satisfy I5 (and I6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Thus the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis because no whole-brain task activation map is available for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol images vs neutral images) in recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients. It reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral), conducts and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-test and multiple regression with FWE correction via AlphaSim; tables and figures described), and provides participant age/sex information, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

The study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI study using visual cues), I4 (within-participant contrasts: cigarette-related and pleasant vs neutral), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM with reported statistical maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables). However it does not satisfy I7 because the MRI scanner field strength is not reported in the provided full text (age/sex, cue type, and processing software are reported). Full text appears complete; therefore exclusion is due to missing required scanner field strength information (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the key modality and stimulus-type inclusion criteria. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (within-participant contrast of cocaine cues > control stimuli is reported), I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and described in text). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (study is not an fMRI study using visual stimuli — it used [15O]H2O PET with script-guided auditory/mental imagery cues, not visual cues or fMRI), and I7 (MRI-specific information such as MRI scanner field strength is not applicable/reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on fMRI visual cue-reactivity.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related and pleasant images (CSD+, CSP+, CS−), reporting within-subject contrasts (CSD+ vs CS−; CSP+ vs CS−). The paper includes group-level whole-brain analyses (referenced in main text and Supplementary Tables S1–S2 and Figures S3–S4), and provides necessary methodological details (participant demographics referenced in Table 1, cue types, 4T MRI field strength, and SPM8 processing). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is an fMRI study of non-drug (monetary) reward-related cue-reactivity using visual cues (arrow cues signaling monetary vs verbal feedback). It includes within-subject contrasts of monetary reward anticipation > verbal-feedback (control) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (mixed-effects two-sample t-tests and within-group effects) with results described in text and figures/supplementary information. Required methodological details are reported (participant age range and sex matching, cue type—monetary reward, 3T scanner field strength, SPM8 processing). Although cues are abstract arrow cues rather than pictures of consumable natural rewards, they are visual reward-predictive stimuli and meet the review’s criteria for visual cue-reactivity. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study meets I3 (fMRI of drug cue-reactivity using visual/audiovisual stimuli) and I4 (within-subject contrast: cocaine cues vs neutral segments). However, it does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps; analyses were limited to a priori neuroanatomic regions (ten ROIs) with regional signal measures and pixel-fraction thresholds. Thus it fails I5 (whole-brain voxelwise result) and consequently I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results). The paper also does not report the processing software (e.g., AFNI/FSL/SPM), so I7 is not fully satisfied. Because the report provides only ROI-based results with no whole-brain maps, exclusion criterion E3 applies. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking-related vs neutral images) with within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral) at two sessions. Analyses used whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM and voxelwise contrasts reported with cluster correction and coordinate tables/figures. Methods report participant age and sex (female, mean age 43.2), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol cues and neutral control images, reporting within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral). The paper presents whole-brain, group-level task activation results (whole-group alcohol>neutral maps and clusterwise thresholds reported; tables/figures/coordinates referenced) and includes participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8/SPM12; AFNI used for cluster correction). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is an fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues (I3), includes a within-participant contrast of heroin-related > neutral stimuli (I4), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (p<.0001 whole-brain cluster-level corrected) with tables/figures (I5,I6), and provides participant age and sex, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).
