This article reports an empirical human fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using audio-visual (visual) smoking and nonsmoking stimuli, with a within-subject contrast (smoking cue > nonsmoking cue). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported using SPM2 with tables/figures of coordinates and SPM images. Participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes an unmasked whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

Full-text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/tabled/figured), I7 (participant info, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does NOT assess drug- or listed natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/food/sexual cues; it uses monetary reward/effort cues), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues > control or natural reward cues > control is reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not examine drug or natural reward cue-reactivity as required (I3) and does not include the required within-subject drug/natural cue>control contrast (I4).

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-participant contrasts ("smoke > control") and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (RFX ANOVA and RFX ANCOVAs) with multiple-comparison correction, and provides coordinates/tables and figures of results. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX 1.10.4) are reported. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues in abstinent heroin-dependent patients, employing within-subject (pre vs post; heroin vs neutral) contrasts and reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2×2 repeated measures ANOVA) with cluster-corrected results and reported coordinates. Participant age/sex, cue type (heroin), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (neutral geometric shapes conditioned to alcohol). It reports within-subject contrasts of CS+ > CS−, performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction, and provides coordinates and detailed methods (scanner field strength, processing software SPM8), and participant age/sex. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only references/metadata provided). From available information: Title and metadata indicate an fMRI study of cue-induced smoking craving in virtual environments, so inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual/virtual stimuli) appears likely met. However, the full text lacks methods/results so I cannot verify: I4 (within-participant drug-cue > control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps), I6 (reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures/text), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type details, scanner field strength, processing software). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are clearly met from the available content. Because core article content (methods/results/discussion) is missing, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria. Marking as excluded due to incomplete full text (fulltext_incomplete=true).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related word cues (cocaine) with a within-subject drug>neutral contrast. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with coordinates and cluster-corrected results (Table 2, figures), and provides participant demographics (age/sex matching described), cue type, scanner field strength (4T), and processing software. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental material is noted but not required. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cues (500 ms images) of drug and comparator stimuli in cocaine-dependent participants, with within-subject contrasts (cocaine > neutral) reported. The paper reports group-level task activation and corrected whole-brain cluster results (Table 2, whole-brain-corrected clusters outside the ROI mask) and shows group task maps in figures, satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. Participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength (3 T) and processing software (SPM8, AFNI, FSL) are all reported. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject food>control contrasts (food vs scrambled control pictures). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain thresholds, FWE corrections, and coordinate tables/figures). Methods report participant age/sex (mean age 24.4±3.4, 13 female), cue type (food), MRI scanner (3T Siemens TRIO) and preprocessing software (SPM5). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used resting-state fMRI and graph-theory connectivity analyses in smokers versus controls, with no task-based cue exposure or visual cue presentation. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (study reports only resting-state analyses without any whole-brain task activation map) and E5 (analyses are group comparisons of connectivity metrics without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a task fMRI study of drug/natural reward cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported), I5 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I6 (no task whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), I7 (although participant age, sex, scanner field strength and processing software are reported, cue type is not applicable/absent). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded for not addressing task-evoked visual cue-reactivity as required by the review.

The study is an empirical fMRI experiment using visual smoking cues in heavy-drinking nondaily smokers and reports within-subject contrasts of smoking vs control cues. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA) with FDR correction and cluster results presented in tables/figures, and provides participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine/smoking), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM2). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine-related (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking>nonsmoking cues (personal and standard environments and proximal cues). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxel-wise task activation analyses (exploratory whole-brain contrasts with cluster correction) with results presented in figures and supplementary tables. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine/smoking), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are all reported. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual alcohol pictures vs. neutral beverages. It includes within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using AFNI (3dLME) with multiple-comparison cluster correction. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (alcohol images), MRI field strength (3.0T), and processing software (AFNI) are reported. Results are presented as whole-brain clusters/tables and figures. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > neutral cues, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects FLAME1, with cluster-thresholding). Results are reported as tables/figures with coordinates. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are all reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study is excluded because it does not assess drug-cue or clearly defined natural reward-related cue-reactivity (e.g., food or sexual cues) as required. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps reported using SPM8 with cluster-corrected results) and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/natural-reward cues; it assesses general emotional IAPS images), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues>control stimuli or natural reward-related cues>control stimuli; contrasts are positive>neutral and negative>neutral for general emotional images), I7 (while age/sex, scanner field strength, and software are reported, the cue type is not one of the required cue categories—nicotine, alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, heroin, food, or sexual—so the required cue-type reporting is not met). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue‐reactivity (video stimuli) contrasting heroin cues vs neutral cues within subjects. The methods describe within-participant contrasts (heroin>neutral A2 vs A1), voxelwise whole-brain, group-level factorial analyses with cluster correction, and results reported as coordinates, figures, and tables. Participant age/sex, cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (AFNI) are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual images. It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking > neutral images and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANCOVA) with cluster-level correction, reporting cluster coordinates and figures. Participant age and sex (women only), cue type (smoking/nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli, with within-subject contrasts of alcohol>neutral and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (satisfied I3, I4, I5, I6). Participant age/sex, cue type, and processing software (AFNI) are reported. However, the manuscript does not report MRI scanner field strength (Tesla), which is required by inclusion criterion I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete. Because I7 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual methamphetamine cues (I3), reports a within-participant contrast of Methamphetamine Cue>Control Cue (I4), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (cluster-corrected Z-statistic images) (I5). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures (I6). Relevant metadata are reported: participant age and sex, cue type (methamphetamine), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL 5.0) (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper includes whole-brain task activation (not ROI-only or connectivity-only), contains within-subject task contrasts (not only between-group contrasts), and is an empirical human fMRI study. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cue stimuli (Alcohol Pictures Task) with within-participant contrasts of alcohol > non-alcohol beverage images. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain ANOVA with cluster correction; Table 3 and Figure 2 provide coordinates/clusters), and provide necessary methodological details: participant ages/sex distribution, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (SPM5 preprocessing, AFNI group analysis). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task activation maps).

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking videos with within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported; processing software (FSL 4.1), cue type (nicotine/smoking), and participant age (23 ± 3 y, N=10) are reported. However the provided full text does not report participant sex and does not specify MRI scanner field strength, so it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I7 (required reporting of age and sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). All other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete. Thus EXCLUDED for failure to meet I7.

This is an fMRI study using visual cannabis cues with an explicit within-subject contrast of cannabis>neutral (I3, I4). Group-level voxelwise results are reported (MNI coordinates in Table 2) and the paper references whole-brain analyses in Online Resource 2 (satisfying I5 and I6). Participant characteristics (sex distribution), cue type (cannabis, sexual, aversive), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported (I7). Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary whole-brain results are indicated. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol cue > neutral; stress > neutral), whole-brain voxel-wise group-level analyses with cluster correction (AFNI 3dClustSim, p<0.001, cluster p<0.05), and provides coordinates and ROI results. Participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio/Prisma), and processing software (BioImageSuite; AFNI used for cluster correction) are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This article reports an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue reactivity using visual stimuli (videos) with within-subject contrasts (Smoking>Food, Smoking>Baseline). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FLAME/cluster correction) with results presented in figures and tables. Methods report participant age/sex, cue types (nicotine and food), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (FSL). All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper) are met. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Inclusion recommended for meta-analysis of fMRI studies of drug and natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it did not use visual stimuli for cue-reactivity. Instead, the paradigm used individualized script-driven guided imagery (auditory/imagery cues). Satisfied inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrasts: drug-cue vs. neutral), I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with family-wise error correction), I6 (whole-brain results are clearly reported and described), and I7 (participant age and sex, cue type [cocaine/alcohol], 3T scanner field strength, and processing software [AFNI] reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded solely because cue modality is not visual, which is essential for this meta-analysis focused on visual cue-reactivity.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues vs neutral/abstract control stimuli with within-subject contrasts (alcohol>control) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses using SPM99 (1.5T scanner). Results are reported as whole-brain task-evoked activations (tables/figures/coordinates) and participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software are provided. The paper includes methods, results, and discussion, and therefore meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol vs non-alcohol beverage images) and reports within-subject ALC>BEV contrasts; participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. However, the paper’s imaging analyses are ROI-based (predefined 6-mm spheres with extracted BOLD timecourses and hierarchical linear models) and the reported results are ROI statistics/tables. No group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps (or whole-brain coordinate tables/figures describing an unmasked whole-brain task effect) are presented in the full text, so it lacks the required whole-brain evidence (I5). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses) and does not meet inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant first-level contrasts of alcohol cues > control stimuli, and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (1-sample t-test, cluster tables/figures). Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and should be included.

This is not a cue-reactivity fMRI study using visual drug or natural reward cues. The study investigates resting-state network coupling and working-memory (N-back) task effects in smokers during abstinence vs satiety; it does not include within-participant contrasts of drug cues > control stimuli or any visual cue-reactivity paradigm. It does report group-level whole-brain task activation maps (N-back) and participant details (age, sex), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (pictures) in alcohol-dependent participants. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol>soft drink (pretraining) and pre-post changes, and group-level voxelwise analyses; whole-brain analyses are described and presented in the online supplement (tables/figures), which satisfies the requirement that whole-brain results may be in supplemental materials. Participant characteristics (all-male sample, group sizes), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary tables/figures are referenced but missing here (acceptable). Therefore study meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and can be included in the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: it did not use visual stimuli for cue-reactivity. The fMRI paradigm used personalized audiotaped imagery (auditory scripts) rather than visual drug or natural reward cues. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrasts: alcohol imagery > neutral), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and reported), I7 (participant demographics, cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio), and processing software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue exposure uses individualized auditory/imagery scripts (guided imagery) rather than visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant alcohol-cue > neutral contrast is reported), I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and corrections are reported), I6 (whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type = alcohol, scanner field strength = 3T, and processing software (AFNI/BioImageSuite/SPM) are reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because the meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli specifically, the use of non-visual, imagined/audio cues disqualifies the study for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study using pseudo-continuous arterial spin-labeled perfusion MRI that examined neural responses to audiovisual smoking cues versus nonsmoking cues in individuals with nicotine use disorder. It includes a within-participant contrast of smoking cues > nonsmoking cues, performed voxelwise in a group-level GLM (whole-brain analysis followed by small-volume correction), and reports significant clusters with peak coordinates and figures. Relevant participant information (sex counts, age controlled as covariate), cue type (nicotine/smoking), MRI field strength (Siemens 3T Trio), and processing software (SPM8, ASL toolbox, MATLAB) are reported. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, with within-subject contrasts (smoking vs neutral) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (including ethnicity × condition interaction maps) reported with coordinates and figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Allegra), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are reported. Although the combined smokers’ main effect smoking>neutral had no significant voxels, the study performed the required within-participant contrast and provides group-level whole-brain statistical maps for task-related effects (interaction), satisfying inclusion requirements. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without whole-brain task map, or non-empirical) are met.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual photographic cues. It reports within-participant contrasts (smoking cues > control cues) and conducts group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses with whole-brain results reported (tables/figures and coordinates) using SPM5 on a 4.0-T scanner. Participant age, sex distribution, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software are all reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) are met. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets all specified inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (juice) with a learned visual cue (CS) and analyses contrasting event types (CS, UCS, PTDE, NTDE), indicating within-participant contrasts of reward-related cues vs other/control events. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (WB and SVC with cluster-correction), and results are presented in text/tables/figures. Scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (AFNI) are specified, and participant demographics (age range, group matching, and referenced Table 1) are reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI of natural reward-related cue with visual stimulus), I4 (within-participant contrasts involving cue vs other/control event regressors), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables), and I7 (age/sex, cue type, scanner strength, and software reported). No exclusion criteria are invoked.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is an fMRI study of drug (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3), reports within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > neutral control stimuli (I4), and provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (main effect smoke>neutral and PPI whole-brain analyses) with cluster-thresholded results reported in tables/figures (I5,I6). Relevant details are reported (participant demographics, cue type, 3T scanner field strength, and processing software FSL) (I7). Although the paper includes seed-based PPI connectivity analyses, it also reports unmasked whole-brain task activations, so exclusion criteria E4 (connectivity-only) do not apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (plus a taste cue) in alcoholic and social-drinking control subjects. It reports a within-participant contrast directly comparing alcohol beverage cues > nonalcohol beverage cues and presents group-level, voxelwise statistical maps derived from spatial normalization and SPM-based cluster analysis (reported in tables/figures). Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (MEDx with SPM99) are reported. Although imaging was limited to anterior brain slices, the paper provides group-level whole-brain (voxelwise within the imaged volume) task-evoked results in tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3–I7. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using an alcohol taste-cue paradigm (gustatory delivery of white wine vs. water) rather than visually-presented drug or natural reward cues. While the study meets several inclusion criteria — I4 (within-subject alcohol>water contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction), I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [FSL] are reported) — it does not satisfy I3 because the primary cue modality is taste, not visual stimulus presentation (visual words indicating the taste were ancillary to the gustatory cue). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study should be excluded from a meta-analysis limited to visual-stimulus cue-reactivity studies.

This is an alcohol cue-reactivity fMRI study using a taste (gustatory) cue paradigm (alcohol vs. water) with visual labels. It includes within-subject Alcohol>Water contrasts, whole-brain group-level analyses, and reports participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software. However, the meta-analysis requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli; the primary cue modality here is taste (gustatory), so it does not meet I3. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cocaine (drug) cue reactivity using visual stimuli. The manuscript reports within-participant GLM contrasts (cocaine cues > neutral cues), a group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis (FLAME 1 mixed-effects) with thresholded statistical maps and cluster results, and provides participant sex/age info, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables (ROIs with MNI coordinates). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without task activation, not non-empirical).

The full text describes an empirical fMRI study in smokers using visual stimuli (cigarette-related and emotional/sexual images). The authors report within-subject whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise analyses including a cigarette>neutral contrast, provide coordinates and cluster statistics (Table 2), and report participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). The paper includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full article content present). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-evoked whole-brain fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli.

This is an fMRI study using visual cues (backward-masked cocaine, sexual, aversive, neutral images) in cocaine-dependent participants. It reports within-participant contrasts (cocaine > neutral, sex > neutral, aversive > neutral) and second-level whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (SPM8) with cluster-corrected thresholds and MNI coordinates. Relevant participant information (male, 18–55), cue types (cocaine, sexual, aversive), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Results include whole-brain statistical maps described in text and tables of peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical, within-subject fMRI cue-reactivity investigation that includes visual smoking cues (videos) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (smoking cue vs fixation) using a 3T scanner and FSL processing. It provides participant age/sex, cue types (alcohol taste and smoking visual), scanner field strength, and software. Although the alcohol cue used a taste paradigm, the smoking task uses visual stimuli and meets the meta-analysis’ requirement for visual cue-based analyses. Whole-brain results are clearly described and illustrated. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue reactivity using visual cue videos. It includes within-participant contrasts (crave-allow vs neutral; crave-resist vs neutral), reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL/FLAME, cluster-corrected Z maps) with coordinates and figures, and provides required methodological details (scanner field strength 1.5T, processing software FSL, cue type nicotine, and demographic/treatment reporting). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core article content is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/food/sexual cues. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and clearly described), I7 (reports participant age/sex, scanner field strength, and processing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an fMRI cue-reactivity study of drug or natural reward-related cues using visual stimuli; it uses a probabilistic delay discounting task with monetary rewards), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli or natural reward-cues > control stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) and reports within-participant contrasts comparing craved food vs control stimuli (Look Craved > Look Not Craved and Look Craved > Look Neutral). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain correction, tables of coordinates and figures). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8, FSL). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity meta-analysis of visual natural rewards.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) with within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts, reported at the group (second)-level using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5). Results are presented as tables of coordinates and figures. Participant age and sex, cue type, scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material not required.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (and visual food and neutral item controls) with within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol>control stimuli and high-risk>low-risk conditions. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FSL, mixed-effects FLAME1; voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction) and whole-brain results/maps are reported and illustrated. Participant age and sex (women 18–28), cue types (alcohol, food, items), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are specified. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3–I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual cues (shapes) in a Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) paradigm to elicit reward-related cue-reactivity (monetary natural reward). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of reward anticipation versus non-incentive (reward>control) and other analogous contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and voxelwise group comparisons are reported (familywise-corrected maps, tables/figures). Methods report participant age/sex, cue type (monetary reward), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (AFNI). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply, and the provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so full text is complete.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts (alcohol > beverage and alcohol > control). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM96/MEDx3.3, thresholded group z maps with cluster correction) and results are presented in text, tables, and figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software are reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study uses a gustatory (taste) cue paradigm (alcohol vs. juice delivered via gustometer), not visual stimuli; therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). It does meet: I4 (within-participant Alcohol>Control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses performed), I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual cigarette cues (video stimuli) in heavy-drinking smokers, reporting within-subject Cigarette Cues > Neutral Cues contrasts. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) with peak coordinates and tables/figures (Tables 2 and 4; Figures 1–6). Methods specify participant age range (21–55), demographic data collection, MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain results are reported, not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues in methadone-maintained patients with within-subject contrasts of heroin-related > neutral stimuli (predose vs postdose and cue>neutral). Group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted using FSL (one-sample and paired t tests) and whole-brain activation maps are reported (figures and text) with ROI masks applied; results are described in the text and figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes whole-brain task activations, empirical human fMRI data). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content is present.

Although this is an fMRI within-subject study using visual monetary cues (reward vs neutral) with adequate participant and scanner details, it does not provide a group-level whole-brain, unmasked task-evoked activation map for the reward>neutral contrast. The main activation results for anticipation were reported using a small-volume (NAcc) correction (ROI), and no whole-brain task activation survived correction or was reported. The paper primarily reports ROI activation results and seed-based (PPI) whole-brain connectivity results. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria for reporting only ROI task analyses without whole-brain task activation (E3) and effectively reports seed-based connectivity without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map (E4). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI with visual natural reward cues — monetary), I4 (within-participant reward>neutral contrast), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, processing software reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported).

This is an fMRI study of cocaine cue reactivity using visual stimuli (videos) with within-subject contrasts of cocaine > food cues. The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (cluster-corrected results described in text and supplemental tables/figures) processed using AFNI on a 3T scanner. Participant age and sex are reported. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3–I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or resting-state analyses, and are empirical human fMRI task activation data. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual drug cue-reactivity.

Excluded because it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis and instead meets exclusion criteria E4 and E5. Specifically: (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 and E5 — the paper reports voxelwise connectivity analyses (ICD and seed-to-voxel connectivity) during guided imagery and does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map; the reported results are between-group connectivity contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain task activation effect. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant age/sex, cue type [food/stress], scanner field strength, and processing software are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (cues were personalized auditory guided imagery, not visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant contrast of visual cues > control stimuli is presented here), and I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is reported). Full text appears complete for screening.

Full text appears to be limited to the abstract only; fulltext_incomplete=true. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of cannabis cue-reactivity using backward-masked visual cannabis cues), I4 (within-participant contrast of cannabis cues > neutral), I5 (reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activations: significant clusters reported with p<.01 and cluster extent), I6 (whole-brain results described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (abstract does not report MRI scanner field strength or processing software; participant age partly reported? sex reported, but key methodological details missing). No exclusion criteria met (E3-E6). Because the full text is incomplete and I7 cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded pending access to full article to verify I7 and other methodological details.

This is not an fMRI study: it is a TMS/EMG study measuring motor-evoked potentials in response to visual smoking cues. Inclusion criterion I3 (functional MRI study) is not met. The study does include a within-participant contrast of smoking cues > scrambled control (I4 met) and reports participant age/sex and cue type, but it provides no MRI scanner field strength, processing software, or any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or coordinate tables (I5, I6, I7 not met). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not meet the required fMRI and whole-brain analysis criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (favorite alcoholic drink images vs water) that reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs water) during a Pavlovian-instrumental transfer task. The paper includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (exploratory whole-brain voxel-wise results reported with coordinates x=18,y=6,z=-12 and pFWE-SVC values) and provides relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (alcohol), MRI scanner field strength (Siemens Trio 3T), and processing software (SPM8). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion E4 applies: the study’s primary analyses use group ICA (a task-based connectivity/network approach) and report network-level modulations rather than unmasked, voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain activation maps (no conventional group-level voxelwise drug>neutral or erotic>neutral SPM-style contrasts are reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task fMRI with visual drug and natural reward cues), I4 (within-participant contrasts derived via component beta-weights drug>neutral and erotic>neutral), and I7 (participant sex/age matching, cue types, scanner field strength 1.5T, and processing software SPM8/GIFT are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map is provided). Therefore exclude under E4.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (participants held and viewed a cigarette vs neutral objects). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (cigarette>neutral) and a group-level, voxelwise mixed-model ANOVA with whole-brain analyses; results are presented as tables of coordinates and figures. Key metadata are reported (participant age and sex, cue type: nicotine, scanner field strength: 1.5T, and processing software: NIS and AFNI). Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, with no exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (videos) and within-subject contrasts (smoking cues > non-smoking cues). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM2 and results reported with coordinates and figures. Participant demographics (age/sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual alcohol-related stimuli (pictures) with detoxified alcohol-dependent patients and matched controls. It includes within-subject contrasts of alcohol cues > neutral cues (CUEalc > IAPSneutral) at the first level and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM/BPM), including whole-brain FWE-corrected results. Relevant metadata are reported (participant age/sex matching, cue type: alcohol, scanner field strength: 1.5 T, processing software: SPM8, BPM, VBM8). Figures/tables provide whole-brain results and coordinates. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies and does not violate exclusion criteria.

Exclusion based on reporting format: The study is an fMRI investigation of cocaine cue-reactivity using visual word stimuli and includes a within-subject cocaine>neutral contrast (meets I3 and I4). It reports methodological details including scanner field strength (3T), processing software (SPM8), and participant demographics referenced in Table 1 (meets I6 and I7). However, the authors’ statistical inference for the cocaine>neutral effect was conducted using a priori ROIs with small-volume correction and no unmasked, whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map is reported for the main contrast. Therefore I5 (whole-brain group-level map) is not met, and the study falls under exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol and non-alcohol beverage pictures) with a within-subject contrast (alcohol > beverage). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses conducted in SPM5 (thresholds and cluster extent reported) and presents results in tables/figures (ventral striatum activation and whole-brain activations). Methods include MRI scanner field strength (Philips 3.0T) and processing software (SPM5). Participant demographics and drinking characteristics are reported (Table 1). Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI investigation of cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (drug, sexual, aversive) in opioid use disorder patients. It reports within-subject contrasts of drug (and other) cues versus neutral stimuli, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (session × stimulus ANOVA with corrected whole-brain results and reported cluster coordinates). Participant age and sex, cue types, scanner field strength (Siemens Tim Trio 3T) and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is present, so the full text appears complete. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI visual cue-reactivity.

Although this is an fMRI study of visual smoking cue-reactivity with within-subject smoking>control contrasts and reports necessary methodological details, the group-level voxelwise analyses were restricted to an a priori mask of cue-related regions rather than a whole-brain, unmasked group-level task activation map. Therefore it fails the whole-brain requirement.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is an empirical fMRI study using visual cue videos for drug (cocaine) and natural reward (food) cue-reactivity (I3); it reports within-subject contrasts of cocaine>neutral and food>neutral (I4); group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM8 with cluster- and FWE-correction are reported (I5) and results are presented in figures/tables (I6); and participant age/sex, cue types, MRI field strength (4T) and processing software (SPM8) are reported (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain task activation maps are provided; results are not limited to ROI/connectivity-only nor are they non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical task fMRI study using visual cues (smoking and food videos) and reports participant age/sex, cue types, scanner strength and processing software (satisfying I3, I4, I7), it does NOT provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for drug>control or natural-reward>control contrasts. The analyses are component/ICA-based (network betas and temporal sorting) and prediction analyses are performed at the component level (DMN, ECN, SN) rather than reporting unmasked voxelwise task activation maps required for meta-analysis. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not met, so the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports fMRI BOLD responses to affective IAPS images and mentions presentation of alcoholic vs neutral beverage images (visual cues), so it meets I3 (fMRI study with visual reward/drug cues). However, the provided full text does not explicitly report a within-participant contrast of drug (alcohol) cues > control stimuli (I4 not demonstrated). It also does not report necessary methodological details required by I7 (scanner field strength and processing software are not provided in the excerpt). While figures and a supplementary table of activations are referenced, the text does not clearly document a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map specifically for alcohol cue reactivity (I5 not confirmed). Therefore not all inclusion criteria are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the available text.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (high-calorie food images) with within-subject contrasts of food>non-food control images. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were reported (exploratory whole-brain comparisons and correlation maps with MNI coordinates and Table 1), and ROI analyses were complemented by whole-brain results. The paper reports participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM99). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cannabis cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (full-color cannabis vs. matched neutral images). The authors report within-participant contrasts of cannabis>control images and present whole-brain group-level results (main effects reported whole-brain corrected, Z>2.3, cluster-corrected P<0.05), with ROI and whole-brain analyses described in text, tables and figures. Participant age/sex info, cue type (cannabis), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject task effects and whole-brain maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article reports an fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol beverage pictures) with within-subject contrasts (alcpic > con). Analyses are whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise tests implemented in SPM8 with cluster correction and activation tables/figures reported. Scanner field strength (3 T), processing software (SPM8), cue type (alcohol), and participant demographics (26 ALC, 26 age-matched controls; demographic details in Table 1) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E5) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study using visual alcohol cues in college students. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol > non-alcohol (and repeated alcohol image contrasts). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were performed and reported (SPM5; cluster-based correction; tables and figures with coordinates and cluster descriptions). Participant age and sex information, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (Siemens 3T Allegra), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues in an alcohol-specific go/no-go task (I3). The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol vs non-alcohol stimuli (e.g., Alcohol_nogo > Non-alcohol_go and interaction contrasts), satisfying a drug-cues > control contrast (I4). Analyses were conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise tests using SPM8 with cluster-level FWE correction (I5). Results are reported in tables and figures and described in the text (I6). Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and software (SPM8) are all reported (I7). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-subject task effects). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual drug cue-reactivity and should be INCLUDED.

This study is an fMRI investigation of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and meets all inclusion criteria: it uses visual alcohol cues (I3), reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > beverage/control stimuli (I4), presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with SPM99 (I5) and reports coordinates/tables/figures of whole-brain results (I6). The paper reports participant sex (male and female college students), cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM99) (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and include whole-brain task activation maps. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of heroin cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It includes a within-subject contrast of heroin-related > neutral cues, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects two-sample t-tests) with multiple-comparison correction (AFNI AlphaSim), and reports results in tables/figures. Relevant participant information (male participants, demographic table), cue type (heroin), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (drug-related) with within-participant contrasts of alcohol-associated versus control (abstract/neutral) stimuli, reported using voxelwise, whole-brain SPM99 analyses (second-level group analyses, thresholds reported) and results presented in tables/figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM99) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, with within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral) during encoding and retrieval. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and corrected for multiple comparisons (FSL, cluster-based threshold); results are reported in figures and Table 2 with MNI coordinates. Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (Siemens Trio 3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines visual smoking cue reactivity and reports within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts and participant/scanner details, but the group-level analyses were restricted to a priori ROI analyses (parameter estimates averaged within 5-mm spheres) rather than reporting an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain coordinates. Therefore it does not meet the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine-related) with within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts (crave and resist conditions). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using FSL/FEAT with FLAME and cluster-thresholded results reported (figures and a cluster/coordinate table). Participant age and sex are reported, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (FSL FEAT v5.98) are provided. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli with a within-participant ALC>BEV contrast and reports participant/scanner/processing details, the analyses and results reported are limited to a priori ROI extractions (right and left ventral striatum percent signal change). The article does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps, coordinate tables, or whole-brain figures that would satisfy the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward). It includes within-participant contrasts (highly desirable > less desirable food images and all food > non-food images) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (paired t-test across subjects) using SPM8 with coordinates and FWE-corrected cluster statistics. Relevant participant information (age, sex), cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity to natural rewards and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study of stress-induced cocaine craving using personalized guided-imagery (auditory/script) stimuli rather than visual drug cues. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps are reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported via coordinates/tables), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type [cocaine-related craving], scanner field strength [1.5T], and processing software are reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (the study does not assess cue-reactivity using visual stimuli — it used script-based guided imagery auditory cues), I4 (there is no within-participant contrast of visual drug cues > control stimuli; contrasts are stress vs neutral imagery). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is ineligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on visual cue-reactivity.

This study is an fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity experiment using visual stimuli and reports within-subject ALC>BEV contrasts (meets I3 and I4). Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported (meets I7). However, the paper presents ROI-based analyses (right ventral striatum % signal change extracted a priori) and does not report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain coordinates in the text, figures, or tables. Therefore it reports only ROI results and violates exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses without whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study using visual marijuana cues in treatment-seeking, marijuana-dependent participants. It reports within-subject contrasts of MJ cues > non-MJ control stimuli and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates, figures, and tables. Methods report MRI field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM2), and participant age/sex are provided. Whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps are described and unmasked data are available online; results are reported in tables/figures (coordinates) and text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual tobacco advertisement stimuli to elicit cue-reactivity. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of tobacco > control advertisements at the first level and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with reported statistical maps, figures, and tables of activations. Participant age and sex (male-only), cue type (nicotine/tobacco), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of heroin cue reactivity using visual (pictorial) stimuli with a within-subject contrast (heroin-related > neutral). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects (FLAME) with cluster correction; results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. Relevant participant info (age, sex: male-only), cue type (heroin), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software (FSL/FEAT) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based analyses with small-volume corrections and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map. Exclusion ID met: E3 (ROI-only analyses). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual cannabis word stimuli), I4 (within-participant cannabis>neutral contrast reported), I7 (participant characteristics, cue type, scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [SPM8] reported). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (no evidence of whole-brain, unmasked voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps; analyses were constrained to a priori ROIs and SVCs). Full text appears complete. Given E3 is satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting several other inclusion criteria.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of functional connectivity in smokers, not a task-based cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports only resting-state analyses without any whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a task fMRI assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug-cues>control contrast), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I6 (no whole-brain task results in any form), I7 (does report participant age/sex and scanner field strength and processing software, but no cue type because no cue task was used — overall the required cue-related reporting for inclusion is absent). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude.

This is an fMRI study using visual food pictures (natural reward) with a within-subject contrast of food>control. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with results summarized in tables and figures, and provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3 (requires cue-reactivity using visual stimuli). This study used a tactile cue-exposure paradigm (marijuana pipe vs pencil). It does meet I4 (within-participant contrast of marijuana cues > control cues), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported as clusters/tables), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity experiment using visual alcohol stimuli (images) with within-subject contrasts ('favourite drinks > neutral') and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (thresholds and cluster coordinates reported). Participant age and sex are given, cue type is alcohol, scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM5) are reported. Results include whole-brain maps/coordinates and ROI analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking-related cues (nicotine) and neutral images with abstinent smokers, reporting participant age/sex, scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM2). The design modeled smoking and non-smoking events, generated subject-level contrasts and conducted a group-level random-effects (whole-brain, voxelwise) analysis (uncorrected p<0.0001, cluster threshold), and reported whole-brain results in text/tables/figures. Although the authors report no significant smoking>neutral differences, the within-participant contrasts were performed and tested at the group level. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and should be included.

Although this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol (a relevant drug cue) and it reports a within-subject alcohol>control contrast using group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinate tables and reports participant age/sex and scanning/processing details, it does NOT meet the review’s required stimulus modality: the paradigm used gustatory (taste) cues (alcohol taste vs litchi) rather than visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol pictures) in alcohol-dependent and control participants. It reports within-participant contrasts of alcohol cues > beverage cues, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; threshold p<=.001, cluster extent) with tables and figures describing activated regions. Methods report scanner field strength (Phillips 1.5T) and processing software (SPM2); demographic information and cue type are described. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures and video). The study reports within-subject contrasts of smoking>neutral cues and group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with reported coordinates and figures (mOFC, NAc, ACC), and also performed ROI analyses. Participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This full-text fMRI study directly addresses the review objective: it assesses nicotine (smoking)-related cue reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes a within-participant contrast of smoking vs. neutral cues (Session contrasts) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (three-way ANOVA) with peak coordinates and activation figures. Relevant metadata are provided: participant sex and age range (male adults), cue type (nicotine/smoking-related images), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM5). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and include task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article is an empirical fMRI study using visual smoking cues (nicotine) and neutral control images with a within-subject contrast (smoking cues > neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level random effects, SPM99) are reported with tables/figures of coordinates and statistical parametric maps. Participant age and sex (10 male, mean age 32), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM99) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation of visual smoking cues in nicotine-deprived smokers and includes within-subject contrasts of smoking-related versus neutral images. Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing approach (custom MATLAB scripts) are reported. However, all reported neuroimaging results derive from predefined region-of-interest (ROI) analyses rather than group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. No unmasked whole-brain activation maps or voxelwise coordinate tables for a whole-brain analysis are presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only study). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs neutral), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level ANOVA with voxelwise thresholding and cluster criteria), and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables. Scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (AFNI) are reported; participant demographic information is indicated (Table 1) including age/sex. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

Although this fMRI study uses visual cues (words 'Alcohol'/'Water') preceding taste delivery, the reported whole-brain analyses and results focus on taste-outcome contrasts (alcohol taste vs. water taste) and prediction-error effects during taste delivery. The paper does not present a within-participant, whole-brain contrast of drug-related visual cues > control visual stimuli (i.e., cue-reactivity to visual stimuli), which is required by the review (I3/I4). The study does meet several other requirements: it reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps (I5), allows coordinate/figure reporting (I6), and provides participant demographics, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (FSL) (I7). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because inclusion criteria I3 and I4 (assessment and reported analysis of visual cue-reactivity contrasts) are not met.

Only the abstract is provided (fulltext_incomplete), so core methods/results are missing. The study appears to be an fMRI CET study with virtual smoking cues (so I3 is likely satisfied). However, the abstract does not report a within-participant cue>control contrast or pre/post cue-specific contrasts (I4 not confirmed), does not specify whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps (I5 not confirmed; I6 cannot be assessed from abstract), and lacks necessary reporting details on scanner field strength and processing software and complete participant demographics (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are explicitly met, but because the full text is incomplete and several inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis at this stage pending full-text availability.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Based on available information: Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI study using visual heroin cues), I4 (within-participant contrast: heroin-visual stimulation vs baseline). Inclusion not verifiable / not met from abstract: I5 (cannot confirm a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or availability of unmasked whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates), I7 (participant age not reported in abstract though sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and software are mentioned). I6 cannot be confirmed (uncertain whether whole-brain results/coordinates or maps are provided). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria (notably I5 and I7) cannot be confirmed, exclude pending full-text access.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that meets all inclusion criteria: visual cues (images signaling impending chocolate milk vs tasteless solution) were used to probe anticipatory/reactivity, within-subject contrasts were computed (anticipation: chocolate milk vs tasteless solution; receipt: chocolate milk vs tasteless solution), and group-level voxelwise (whole-brain) random-effects analyses were performed (SPM8; results thresholded and reported with small-volume correction and whole-brain reporting; coordinates/tables referenced). Relevant participant demographics (age range, sex matching), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T GE), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group without task effect, and is empirical human fMRI). Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The article reports an fMRI study in alcohol-dependent participants using visual alcohol cues (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages and alcoholic vs scrambled baseline), satisfying within-participant cue>control contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps were generated and corrected for multiple comparisons (Monte Carlo FWE), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), 3T scanner field strength, and processing software (AFNI) are reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and supplementary figures/tables; thus full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject contrasts and whole-brain task activation maps). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of visual drug cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

Full text is unavailable (page error). Cannot verify whether study used fMRI visual cue-reactivity, within-participant contrasts, or reported whole-brain voxelwise task maps and required participant/scanner details. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be confirmed: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7.
