No exclusion criteria could be confirmed (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical), so exclusion criteria applied: none. Full text incomplete, so study must be excluded from the meta-analysis pending retrieval of the full article.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts (smoke vs rest/neutral), reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise maps, thresholded and described), and provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (Turbo-BrainVoyager for real-time, SPM8 offline). Whole-brain results are described and illustrated in figures/supplement. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so is complete for screening purposes.

This study used resting-state fMRI and seed-based functional connectivity analyses relating alexithymia to craving; it did not present task-based visual drug or natural reward cues nor report any within-participant drug-cue>control contrast. Therefore it lacks any task-evoked whole-brain activation maps required for cue-reactivity meta-analysis. Exclusion ID met: E4 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (not an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant drug-cues>control contrast), I5 (no task-evoked group-level whole-brain voxelwise map), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain task results to report), I7 (although participant age/sex and scanner field strength are reported, the primary required cue/stimulus information and task details for cue-reactivity are absent). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Consequently the study is not eligible for inclusion in the specified meta-analysis.

Only the abstract and references are provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). The abstract indicates an fMRI study using visual drug-related movie cues (heroin), so inclusion criterion I3 appears satisfied. However, the available text does not provide the full methods/results needed to verify: I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli) cannot be confirmed; I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map) cannot be confirmed; I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results) cannot be confirmed; I7 (participant age/sex, cue type details, scanner field strength, processing software) are not reported in the abstract. None of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be determined from the abstract either. Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be verified, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an fMRI study that used visual alcohol and soft-drink cues and reported within-subject contrasts comparing alcohol vs neutral (soft-drink) conditions (via the approach-alcohol vs approach-soft-drink interaction and separate approach/avoid contrasts). Group-level, voxelwise analyses were performed and whole-brain results are reported (Supplementary Table S1), and ROI SVC results are described; participant age and sex (male), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria were met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task activation maps, empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. The authors report within-subject contrasts of food > control pictures, performed whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM5 with reported thresholding and coordinates (tables/figures). Participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text appears incomplete (only acknowledgments and references provided). Cannot verify key methodological details required by inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met (cannot be confirmed from provided content): I3 (uncertain whether this is a functional MRI study with visual food cues—title implies but methods/results absent), I4 (no evidence of within-participant cue>control contrasts), I5 (no evidence of group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I6 (no reporting of whole-brain results in any form), I7 (no participant demographics, cue type details, scanner field strength, or processing software reported). Exclusion criteria met: none specifically, but exclusion by default due to incomplete/full-text absence of necessary information. Recommendation: obtain full article (methods/results) to reassess.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (drug words) and neutral control words, with within-subject contrasts (drug vs. neutral) and medication vs. placebo conditions. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds) with tables/coordinates and figures (Table 1, Fig. 1) and describes MRI field strength (4T) and processing software (SPM2). Participant demographics (age, sex/gender) and cue type (cocaine) are reported. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7, and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a within-subjects fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity that includes visual stimuli and contrasts of food versus control (nonfood) and high-ED versus low-ED foods. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM5 with reported cluster thresholds and coordinate tables/figures. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (1.5T), and processing software are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (video) and a mosaic control. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (alcohol vs mosaic) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results (clusters reported with FDR correction and coordinates). Methods provide MRI field strength (1.5T) and processing software (BrainVoyager), and demographic info (age, sex) are reported. These meet all required inclusion criteria for visual drug-cue fMRI studies (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and includes whole-brain task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E4 met: the study reports seed-based functional connectivity (FC) maps and ROI-based activation measures but does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for a within-subject contrast of smoking cues > control (no voxelwise smoking>control activation maps or coordinate tables for task activation are shown). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-participant comparisons of smoking cues vs control images/blocks were performed), and I7 (participant sex/age information, cue type [nicotine], scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [SPM8] are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported). Therefore exclude under E4. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: (I3) It is an fMRI study assessing drug cue reactivity using visual stimuli (drug words presented during fMRI); (I4) it includes within-participant contrasts (drug > fixation and drug > neutral word contrasts); (I5) group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (authors report testing whole-brain diagnosis × DAT1 interactions with voxelwise FWE correction); (I6) whole-brain results are described in the text (with reference to whole-brain interaction testing and ROI extraction) and likely reported in figures/tables; (I7) relevant methodological details are provided (scanner field strength = 4T, processing software = SPM8, cue type = cocaine, participant sex counts reported and demographic details referenced in Table 1). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: the paper does not report only ROI or connectivity analyses and contains original empirical human fMRI data with whole-brain task effects. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (drug) cue-reactivity using an alcohol>neutral within-subject contrast (reported as “alcohol-neutral stimuli”), meeting the review’s target. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses with cluster-wise results and coordinates (p<0.001 uncorrected, cluster size thresholds), plus figures and tables of results. Results are presented as whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (coordinates/tables/figures acceptable per I6). Participant characteristics and cue type (alcohol) are reported in the text/tables; acquisition and analysis details are referenced in the methods/supplementary material. Core article sections (intro, methods, results, discussion) are present; only supplementary acquisition/processing details are in supplement (acceptable). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of visual smoking cues with within-subject SCs vs NCs contrasts, reporting participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (1.5T) and processing software (SPM2). However, the authors report results obtained within an a priori fronto-limbic mask (WFU PickAtlas) rather than presenting an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. The meta-analysis requires at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task effect (I5), which is not provided here. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study cannot be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using dynamic visual stimuli (movie scenes). It includes a within-participant contrast of smoking>control scenes, reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects activation maps (thresholds and coordinates), and provides required participant demographics, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject alcohol>beverage contrasts and participant/scanner/processing details. However, all reported analyses are ROI-based (extraction of BOLD timecourses and ROI HLM/GLMs); no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, coordinate tables, or whole-brain figures are reported. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task map) and I6 (no acceptable reporting of whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI investigation using visual cues (images indicating monetary reward, cigarette puffs, or neutral) and includes within-participant contrasts (puff>neutral; money>neutral). Participant age/sex, cue types (nicotine and monetary), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. However, the analyses and reported results are restricted to a priori regions-of-interest in the ventral/dorsal striatum and the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting) and does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual stimuli and meets all inclusion requirements: it uses visual smoking cues, reports within-participant smoking cue > control cue contrasts, and performs group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses with results reported as tables/figures/coordinates. Relevant participant details (age/sex), cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software (SPM2) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

Study is an fMRI investigation of smoking (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli and reports within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > neutral cues. The methods describe a whole-brain random-effects GLM (voxelwise) contrast for smoking>neutral and present task-evoked activation maps/figures (with comment on multiple-comparison correction). Relevant metadata are reported: all-male smoker sample (demographics referenced), cue type (nicotine/smoking images), 3T MRI scanner field strength, and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study used olfactory (ethanol odor) cues rather than visual stimuli. The meta-analysis requires studies that assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3), which is not met. The study does meet the other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant contrast: ethanol odor > neutral air), I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type [alcohol], MRI field strength [1.5T], and processing software [SPM] reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded solely because it does not use visual stimuli as required (I3 not met).

This study is a resting-state functional connectivity (RSFC) seed/ROI analysis comparing opioid-using vs non-using psychiatric inpatients. It does not assess cue-reactivity to visual drug or natural reward stimuli, contains no within-participant task contrast of drug-cues > control stimuli, and reports no task-evoked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level activation maps. Therefore it fails the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criterion E4 (resting-state/seed-based connectivity without whole-brain task activation).

This empirical fMRI study used visual heroin-related cues (24 heroin pictures vs 24 neutral) in an event-related cue-reactivity task and modeled drug versus neutral at first-level, satisfying a within-participant contrast (heroin>neutral). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level analyses are reported (activations reported at P<0.001 uncorrected with tables/figures), and whole-brain results are described in text and tables. Participant age and sex (male-only), cue type (heroin), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without task map, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food/chocolate) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures of chocolate). It includes within-participant contrasts of cue>control (chocpic vs. grey control) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2), with peak coordinates and figures for activations. Relevant metadata are provided: participant sex and age range (all female, 20–30 years), cue type (food/chocolate), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM2). Results include whole-brain and small-volume corrected statistics, suprathreshold peaks, and correlation analyses. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group without task effect, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7.

The study is excluded because it does not use visual stimuli for cue-reactivity (I3 not met). It does meet other inclusion criteria: I4 (within-participant AO>control contrasts), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/text), and I7 (participant demographics, cue type, 3T scanner, and SPM5 reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded due to failure to meet I3 (visual-stimulus requirement).

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (ALC images) with a within-subject ALC>BEV contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (second-level GLM) and reported with cluster-level FWE correction and MNI coordinates (figures/tables provided). Participant demographics (age range, sex distribution), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for extraction. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study clearly investigates alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (meets I3), reports within-subject contrast alcohol>neutral (meets I4), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (meets I5) and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures described in the text (meets I6). It reports participant ages, cue type (alcohol), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5), but the full text provided does not report participant sex or sex distribution. Because inclusion criterion I7 requires relevant information on participant age AND sex, I7 is not satisfied based on the supplied content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I7 (missing sex information).

Although this is an fMRI study using visual alcohol and food stimuli (I3) and it reports group-level whole-brain task results (win>lose) with coordinates (satisfying I5 and I6) and provides participant demographics, cue types, scanner field strength and processing software (I7), the paper does NOT report a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli (I4 not met). The analyses focus on reward (win>lose) and personal-reference (high vs low) contrasts, and stimulus-category effects were tested but no explicit alcohol>control whole-brain cue-reactivity contrast is presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 required for the cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs control videos). It includes within-subject contrasts of smoking>control (averaged across runs and sessions) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise t-maps (thresholded with random field theory) with peak coordinates and tables of results. The paper provides participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine/smoking videos), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (fmristat). Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria E3–E6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (novel geometric CS). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of CS+ vs CS− (CS+ > CS− and CS− > CS+), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with corrected cluster statistics and coordinate reporting, and provides participant age/sex, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (SPM5). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-related cues (images) to assess cue-reactivity in a within-subject design. It reports within-participant contrasts of cue conditions (each condition vs. baseline) and the main contrasts (prayer vs. passive/news) at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded clusters, tables and figures are reported; supplementary tables/figures referenced). Methods report participant demographics (age/sex summarized), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (Siemens Allegra 3T), and preprocessing/analysis software (SPM8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the study assessed cue-reactivity using gustatory (taste) alcohol cues delivered via a gustometer (alcohol vs. litchi juice), not visual alcohol cues. Although written CT/CCT statements were presented visually, the critical cue contrast tested was alcohol taste>control, so the stimulus modality required by the meta-analysis (visual cues) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant alcohol cues > control cues contrast present), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using mixed-effects FLAME with cluster correction), I6 (whole-brain results reported and described), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type [alcohol taste], scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [FSL] reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol-related cues and non-alcohol beverage controls, reporting within-subject contrasts (alcohol > beverage) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA, one-sample t-tests) with tables/coordinates. Scanner field strength (1.5 T), processing software (AFNI), cue type (alcohol), and participant matching by age/sex are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task maps, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This paper reports an fMRI study using visual picture cues (alcohol, marijuana, polydrug, emotional) in college participants and includes within-subject contrasts comparing drug-related cues to neutral controls (e.g., alcohol>neutral, polydrug>neutral, marijuana>neutral). Analyses were conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps using FSL (FEAT) and results are reported in tables and figures. The manuscript provides participant age and sex, cue types, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, reports task activation maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images) and reports within-subject contrasts of food cues versus non-food control stimuli and high-calorie versus low-calorie. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (FWE-corrected maps, figures, and tables), and whole-brain voxel-based correlation analyses with plasma measures are included. The manuscript provides participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3 T), and processing software (BioImageSuite/AFNI/SPM references). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This fMRI study examines neural repetition priming for alcohol, polydrug, and marijuana visual cues in high-risk college students and reports whole-brain, voxelwise BOLD results using FSL. However, it does not include a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli (or natural reward cues > control) required for cue-reactivity analyses; instead, contrasts are non-studied versus studied (repetition priming). Also, the report does not provide all required participant and scanner metadata (age reported only as 'college students' without numeric ages; scanner field strength is not given in this full text and is referred to the accompanying main study). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I4 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used resting-state fMRI to compare KB220Z™ vs placebo in abstinent heroin users and did not examine cue-reactivity to visual drug or natural reward cues. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports participant age and sex, cue type = heroin, MRI field strength = 3T, and processing software = SPM5). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a task-based fMRI study of visual reward/drug cue reactivity), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug-cues>control stimuli), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an rtfMRI cue-reactivity study using visual smoking images (I3) with within-participant contrasts of smoking cues versus rest/neutral (I4). Participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (SPM8) are reported (I7). However, the paper reports analyses focused on individually defined ROIs (ACC) and ROI-based percent signal change; it does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or tables/coordinates/figures of whole-brain results required for meta-analysis. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting) and fails inclusion criteria I5 (whole-brain group-level map) and I6 (no whole-brain results reported in acceptable form). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of smoking (nicotine) cue reactivity using visual stimuli with within-subject contrasts of smoking cues vs control stimuli (I3, I4 met) and reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software (I7 met). However, the study reports only ROI-based analyses and explicitly states exclusive use of ROI-based fMRI analyses with no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or coordinate tables (E3). Therefore it fails to meet the required whole-brain analysis criterion (I5 not met). No whole-brain results are provided in text, tables, or figures (I6 not met). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to E3 (only ROI analyses; no whole-brain task-evoked maps).

This study does not assess drug- or natural reward–related cue-reactivity using visual reward/drug cues. Instead it reports fMRI of aversive fear conditioning with visual CS (colored squares) predicting an electrical shock. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported) and I6 (whole-brain results are described in text/tables/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a functional MRI study of drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual reward/drug stimuli), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward cues > control stimuli), and I7 (cue type is aversive/pain-predicting stimuli, not one of the required reward/drug cue types). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI study that used visual alcohol-related cues (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages) (I3). The methods describe within-participant contrasts (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverage pictures) and generation of individual and group-level statistical maps for each contrast (I4). Analyses were voxel-wise and group-level t-tests were performed (whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps) (I5). Results and methods reporting meet acceptable formats (text/figures; some stimulus contrasts reported in text and other contrasts noted as computed even if not shown) (I6). Relevant participant and technical details are reported: ages (21–65), sex/demographics in Table 1, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI) (I7). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Although the alcohol>neutral group-level map is not presented in detail in the Results (noted as "data not shown"), the paper documents that voxelwise group analyses for the alcohol cue contrast were computed, supporting inclusion.

This study is excluded because it does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual cues (INCLUSION I3 and I4 not met). It is a reinforcement-learning fMRI study using abstract stimuli and feedback (smiling/frowning faces), not a cue-reactivity paradigm with alcohol or other reward images. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported) and I6 (whole-brain results are reported/described with coordinate information). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (fMRI cue-reactivity using visual drug/natural reward stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or natural reward-related cues > control stimuli). I7 (detailed reporting of cue type relevant to cue-reactivity) is also not satisfied because no drug/natural reward cue type is used. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are applicable.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) with within-subject contrasts (food > nonfood). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise (whole-brain) analyses (voxel-wise subtraction, figures showing whole-brain maps) and provides coordinates/tables and figures; methods report scanner field strength (3.0T) and processing software (AFNI), and participant age/sex are described. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol and affective IAPS images). It reports within-participant contrasts (alcohol>neutral; positive>neutral; negative>neutral). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM5; coordinates/tables/figures provided). Participant age and sex are reported (12 patients, 12 controls; sex and ages given), cue types (alcohol, positive/negative affective images), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM5) are specified. The paper is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of alcohol cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (alcohol pictures) with a within-subject contrast (alcohol > neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM5/SPM8) with cluster-corrected results and coordinates in tables/figures. Participant age range and sex are reported; scanner field strength (3T) and processing software are specified. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is a behavioral cue-reactivity experiment using personalized videotaped alcohol cues and measures self-reported urge; it does not include any functional MRI data or analyses. Therefore it fails the core fMRI-related inclusion criteria: I3 (not an fMRI study), I4 (no within-participant fMRI contrast of drug cues > control), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), I6 (no whole-brain results to report in any format), and I7 (no MRI scanner field strength or processing software reported). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete for the purposes of screening (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text provided is only a brief summary/abstract. It confirms an fMRI study using alcohol-related visual cues (I3 met) but does not provide sufficient methodological detail to confirm: (I4) a within-participant drug-cues > control-stimuli contrast, (I5) a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map, (I6) whether whole-brain results were reported in tables/figures/supplement, or (I7) participant age/sex, scanner field strength, and processing software. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confidently applied from the summary alone. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot verify required whole-brain reporting and participant/method details, so the study must be excluded pending full-text retrieval.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with a within-subject smoking>neutral contrast, group-level whole-brain analyses (cluster-corrected Z=2.3, p<0.05) reported with coordinates and figures, and full reporting of participant demographics, cue type, scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). The full-text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study used PET (H2^15O) neuroimaging, not functional MRI. Inclusion criterion I3 requires an fMRI study; because imaging modality is PET, the study does not meet I3 and must be excluded. The study does meet other applicable criteria: it includes within-participant contrasts of drug video > neutral video (I4), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM activation maps (I5), provides results in figures/tables described in text (I6), and reports participant demographics, cue type (heroin), and processing software (SPM) (I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map required for inclusion (E3). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual smoking images), I4 (within-participant contrast of smoking cues > neutral/control images), and I7 (reports participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no evidence of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported in the main text, tables, figures, or supplements). The full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion; however the analyses are ROI-focused (spheres centered on meta-analytic coordinates) and supplemental materials do not present an unmasked whole-brain task map, so the study must be excluded under E3.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is an empirical human functional MRI study of drug (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual (audio-visual video) stimuli; it reports within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > non-smoking control cues; analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction and reported peak coordinates; results and coordinates are reported in the text/figures; and participant demographics (age range, sex), cue type, scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes unmasked whole-brain task effects, and is empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (core content present), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study using visual monetary cues (MID task) to probe nondrug reward-related cue-reactivity. It includes within-subject contrasts of reward cues versus nonincentive cues (pre-response $1/$10 vs $0), group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (3dMEMA, FDR-corrected), and reports participant age/sex, cue type (monetary), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a within-subject event-related fMRI study of visual drug (smoking) cues with reported participant age/sex, cue type (nicotine), scanner field (1.5T), and processing software (SPM99) — so it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I7. However, all reported neuroimaging analyses are ROI-based (mean BOLD within predefined ROIs) and no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps, coordinates, or unmasked whole-brain results are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (and the related reporting allowance I6), and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Because fulfilling ALL inclusion criteria is required, the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (alcoholic beverage images) and non-alcoholic control images in alcohol-dependent patients and controls. The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing alcoholic versus non-alcoholic beverage cues (e.g., alcohol cues > non-alcohol cues for positive images) and other task-evoked contrasts. Analyses are voxel-wise, group-level, whole-brain statistical maps (voxel-wise t-tests, cluster correction) with tables/figures of clusters. Relevant details are reported: participant sex/age matching, cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in alcohol-dependent patients using visual alcohol cues (AAT) and control (soft drink) cues, satisfying the review objective. It includes within-participant contrasts of drug cues versus control (e.g., [alcohol pull > soft drink pull]) at the group level. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (whole-brain results reported in text/supplement and one peak surviving whole-brain FWE), and results are described in the manuscript (with supplementary whole-brain maps/tables referenced). Participant sex (male-only), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli, with within-subject smoking>neutral contrasts and group-level whole-brain analyses reported (tables/figures/coordinates). Scanner field strength (1.5T) and processing software (SPM5) are specified. However, the full text does not report participant sex (nor clear participant age summary statistics); only eligibility age range is given. Inclusion criterion I7 (reporting participant age and sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software) is therefore not fully met. All other inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Because I7 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis per the protocol.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the cue-reactivity paradigm used individualized, script-driven guided imagery (auditory/internal imagery), not visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant contrasts of alcohol cue vs neutral/control were reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps with familywise correction), I6 (whole-brain results are clearly reported in text/figures/tables), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type [alcohol], scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [AFNI/SPM/BioImageSuite] are provided). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because the meta-analysis specifically requires visual-stimulus cue paradigms (I3), this study must be excluded despite otherwise meeting other criteria.

The study is excluded because it is not an fMRI study of neural cue-reactivity but a behavioral cue-reactivity experiment using self-report craving and mood measures. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none (no exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply). (b) Inclusion IDs met: None of I3–I7 are satisfied. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (not a functional MRI study), I4 (no within-participant fMRI contrast drug-cues>control), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported), I6 (no whole-brain neuroimaging results in tables/figures), I7 (no MRI scanner field strength or processing software reported). Additionally, the provided full text appears limited to abstract/metadata rather than full article content, so fulltext_incomplete=true.

Although this is an fMRI study using visual cigarette and food cues with group-level whole-brain analyses and adequate reporting of participants, cue types, scanner, and processing (I3, I5, I6, I7 met), it does NOT present a within-participant contrast of drug cues > control (neutral) stimuli or natural reward cues > neutral control as required (I4 not met). The reported analyses focus on cognitive regulation contrasts (LATER vs NOW) and correlations/mediation involving regulation success; the main effect of cue type (cigarette vs food) is stated as not discussed and not presented in detail. No neutral control stimuli contrast (drug>neutral) is provided in the full text. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet all inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual smoking images (I3). It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking cues > neutral cues (I4) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (FDR-corrected activations and whole-brain regression/PPI results) and figures/coordinates (I5, I6). Participant age and sex (young male smokers and matched nonsmokers), cue type (nicotine), MRI field strength (3T Philips), and processing software (SPM8, FSL) are all reported (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (study includes whole-brain task activation maps and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This empirical study used fMRI (with concurrent EEG group) to assess nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (smoking vs neutral pictures) within participants, and reports whole-brain task-evoked analyses (2×2 ANOVA, FWE-corrected activations with coordinates). Participant demographics (age comparison and sex distribution) and cue type are reported; scanner acquisition and preprocessing details are referenced in the fMRI data acquisition/preprocessing subsection and Supporting Information (supplementary materials included). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual smoking cue videos (nicotine) with within-participant contrasts (smoking videos > control videos). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed (FLAME, TFCE-corrected) and whole-brain activation results are reported in the text/figures/tables. Relevant participant information (age, sex), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (FSL) are provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task map, or non-empirical) are met.

This publication is a narrative review of functional neuroimaging (fMRI and MRS) studies in drug abusers and does not report original empirical fMRI data. Exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original human fMRI data) applies. No original within-participant drug-cue > control contrast is reported as a primary analysis (I3 and I4 not met). The paper does not provide a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from an original experiment (I5 not met). Required primary-study details for inclusion (participant age/sex per primary dataset, cue type tied to an original analysis, scanner field strength, processing software) are not provided as results of an original fMRI experiment (I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4, I5, I7. Full text appears complete (contains intro, methods of review, results, discussion, references), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with individualwithin-subject contrasts of food>neutral and group-level voxelwise analyses. The manuscript includes whole-brain exploratory analyses (1-sample t test, FWE-corrected, reported clusters; Figures and Tables report task-evoked maps), as well as ROI analyses; participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using visual natural reward-related cues (images of a $100 bill vs a blurry rectangle) and reports within-subject contrasts of reward>nonreward. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and thresholded (z>3.1, cluster p<.05) with results reported in tables/figures. Participant age and sex, cue type (money reward), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study that includes visual alcohol cue stimuli (90 pictures of alcoholic and neutral beverages), reports within-subject contrasts (alcoholic vs non-alcoholic beverages), and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI 3dMVM, cluster-based FWE correction reported). Participant age and sex (females 21–65), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3T, multiple vendors), and processing software (AFNI) are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject task activation maps). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts (all food > non-food; high-calorie > low-calorie), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and cluster coordinates, and provides participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports voxelwise analyses restricted to an a priori ROI mask (not an unmasked, whole-brain group-level activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of nicotine cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (within-subject smoking-cue > control-cue contrast was created), I6 (peak coordinates and cluster locations are reported), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength [3T], and processing software [SPM8] are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain, unmasked voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported; analyses were restricted to an ROI mask). Full text appears complete.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an fMRI study of nicotine (cigarette) cue-reactivity using visual/object cues (I3). The analysis includes within-participant contrasts comparing cigarette versus control cue (cigarette>control) and reports a main effect of cue (I4). Group-level whole-brain, voxelwise activation maps were computed and thresholded (cluster-corrected), with results reported as coordinates and figures (I5, I6). Required methodological details are provided: participant age and sex (male, 18–45), cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3-Tesla), and processing software (AFNI, FSL, etc.) (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical limitations). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual Pavlovian cues and food images. The study includes within-subject contrasts of food-outcome cues vs. a no-outcome control cue and reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses (permutation-based voxelwise testing; exploratory whole-brain results referenced). Participant age/sex, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a clinical pilot study assessing heroin craving via self-report (VAS) in methadone-maintained patients; it does not involve functional MRI, nor a visual cue-reactivity paradigm. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI study using visual stimuli), and consequently also fails I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5/I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or coordinate/figure-reported whole-brain results), and I7 (no MRI scanner field strength or processing software reported). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are specifically triggered. Exclude for not meeting required fMRI/cue-reactivity inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (no-go unhealthy food vs go healthy food; analyses collapsing food cues) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (3dMVM) with tables/figures of significant clusters. Relevant participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (Siemens 3T), and processing software (AFNI, ANTs, AFNI 3dMVM, SPSS) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-subject task activation maps). Full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food images (natural reward cues) and meets all inclusion criteria. It uses within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood (food vs nonfood) across sessions, reports group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates and t-values for activated clusters, and also reports whole-brain regression results (FWE-corrected) for parametric modulation. Participant age and sex (young adult males), cue type (food), MRI scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study used fMRI and presented tobacco images during a Smoking Pleasantness task (I3) and reports group-level whole-brain maps (for the interoceptive attention task) with coordinates (I5, I6) and participant demographics and cue type (I7). However, there is no reported within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli or a whole-brain, task-evoked cue-reactivity analysis: imaging analyses focus on an interoceptive attention task and resting-state connectivity, not a voxelwise cue-reactivity contrast. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4 and cannot be included in the cue-reactivity meta-analysis.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is an fMRI study of drug cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (I3: methamphetamine cue pictures); it includes a within-participant contrast of Methamphetamine Cue > Control Cue (I4); it reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps with cluster-corrected Z-statistic images (I5) and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables (I6); and it reports participant age/sex, cue type (methamphetamine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL) (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task whole-brain activation maps, and is empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli with within-participant smoking>neutral contrasts and adequate reporting of participant demographics and scanner/processing details. However, the neuroimaging results are reported primarily as ROI-based analyses (PCC) and the only voxel-wise group analysis was restricted to the PCC (small-volume/ROI-restricted analysis). There is no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map or whole-brain coordinates/figures described that would satisfy a whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map requirement. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only reporting).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food) with within-subject contrasts (hedonic food images > nonfood objects). Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise random-effects maps (voxel-wise p<0.01, cluster-level FDR q<0.05) reported in figures and tables of coordinates. Relevant participant information (age range, sex distribution), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes unmasked task effects). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study is not an fMRI task activation study. It reports EEG/ERP (LORETA) cue-reactivity and DTI/fiber-tracking results following tDCS in alcohol and crack-cocaine users, but does not provide any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise fMRI task-evoked statistical maps for drug- or natural reward-related visual cue contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (relevant participant and imaging acquisition details reported: male participants, cue types, MRI scanner field strength for DTI, processing software for EEG/DTI). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not a functional MRI study assessing cue-reactivity), I4 (no documented within-participant fMRI contrast of drug cues>control stimuli), I5 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI activation maps). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) specifically apply, but failure to meet the required fMRI-related inclusion criteria mandates exclusion.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation using visual drug-cue stimuli (drug-related pictures) with within-subject contrasts of drug cues > neutral cues. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps (main effect thresholded at p < .05 FWE) and provides whole-brain exploratory results (coordinates/figures). Participant age and sex (male adolescents, ages 14–19), cue type (stimulants/cocaine/methamphetamine/drug paraphernalia), MRI field strength (1.5T mobile Siemens Avanto), and processing software (SPM12) are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an empirical fMRI investigation of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (pictures). It reports within-participant contrasts of smoking versus matched control (teeth-brushing) stimuli (e.g., BEGIN: S2-T2, END: S4-T4) at the first level and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM5 with reported activations/deactivations (tables/figures described). Participant sex information and age-group comparisons are reported, scanner field strength (1.5 T) and processing software (SPM5) are specified. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Based on this, the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (video clips). It reports within-subject contrasts of smoking vs. non-smoking videos (smoking>non-smoking), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using FSL (FLAME1) with thresholded Z-statistic maps and tables. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is nicotine, scanner field strength (3T Siemens Trio) and processing software (FSL 5.0.9) are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (images). It includes within-participant food>nonfood contrasts in a randomized, within-subject design and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected maps showing visual cortex differences). The paper provides participant age/sex details, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of visual drug-related cues (smoking) using a cue-exposure paradigm with within-subject contrasts (smoking > neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM8) with FDR correction and results reported in text/tables/figures. Participant characteristics (male sample, ages reported in Table 1), cue type (nicotine/smoking), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8, FSL for DTI) are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward (food) cues with within-subject contrasts of food>non-food, reporting whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (tables/figures) analyzed with SPM2 on a 1.5T scanner. Participant sex is reported and participant ages are likely provided in Table 1 (subject characteristics) referenced in the full text; cue type (food), scanner field strength, and processing software are explicitly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual presentation (participants held a cigarette and viewed a live video feed). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of cigarette > control cues (main effect of cue) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables/figures and cluster-correction details. Relevant participant demographics (age range, sex distribution), cue type (cigarette/nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI, FSL, AIR, NIS) are reported. Full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of cigarette (nicotine) cue-reactivity using visual smoking images. The study reports within-subject contrasts comparing smoking-cue trials to control (no-distractor) and neutral trials, and conducts group-level, voxel-wise whole-brain analyses (random-effects repeated-measures ANOVA) with reported cluster thresholds. Results are presented as activation maps and tables with Talairach coordinates; figures and tables report whole-brain clusters. Participant age and sex distribution, cue type (nicotine), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Thus it meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of food (natural reward) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (meets I3) and includes within-participant food-vs-control contrasts (meets I4). However, the paper reports ROI and system-level ROI analyses (VS, OFC, and aggregated ROIs) and does not present or report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or tables of whole-brain peak coordinates in the provided full text. Therefore it meets Exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Additionally, the manuscript as provided does not explicitly report participant ages (only ‘undergraduate students’), so inclusion criterion I7 is not clearly satisfied. Full text appears complete. Exclusion reason: E3 (ROI-only results). Included: I3, I4. Not met: I5 (whole-brain voxelwise group map) and I7 (explicit age information).

This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It includes within-participant contrasts of food>nonfood images, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (flexible factorial and two-sample t tests in SPM8) with tables/figures of activations. Methods report participant age and sex, cue type (food), 3.0T scanner field strength, and processing software (SPM8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of visual food cues with within-subject contrasts (food>control) and group-level whole-brain task results reported (exploratory whole-brain threshold, cluster coordinates/tables). Participant demographics (age, sex), cue type (food), and scanner field strength (3T) are reported. However, the full text does not explicitly report which fMRI processing/statistical software was used (e.g., SPM, FSL, AFNI) for image preprocessing and first-/second-level analyses; only stimulus presentation software (Presentation) and non-imaging stats software (HLM, SPSS) are named. Because inclusion criterion I7 (reporting processing software) is not satisfied, the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. If the authors’ MRI processing software were clearly reported or could be confirmed from supplementary material, the study would likely qualify for inclusion.

Full text is an observational/psychometric study without any fMRI cue-reactivity experiment or task activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast reported), I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise statistical maps), I6 (no whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures for task activation), I7 (while participant age/sex are reported, there is no information on cue type, MRI field strength, or processing software). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is ineligible for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-subject contrasts (high-calorie food > brick walls). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM5 and reported with cluster/voxel results and figures. Relevant participant demographics (ages, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although sample size is small (n=3, leptin-deficient patients), this does not violate inclusion criteria. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (appetizing food images) with a within-subject contrast of appetizing > bland foods. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level SPM{t} maps are reported (thresholds and coordinates provided; Table 1 and figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence. The paper reports participant age range and sex breakdown, cue type (food), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM5). Although the study also includes PPI connectivity analyses, it additionally reports standard task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts, so it does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-subject task effects). Full-text methods, results, and discussion are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual food cues (natural rewards) with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie foods vs objects and low-calorie vs objects). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain exploratory analyses are reported (cluster-corrected maps and peak coordinates in Table 4), meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (FSL, FreeSurfer, ANTs, FEAT) are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3–I7 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete: provided content is a website privacy/cookie notice and article metadata only (title, authors, journal, DOI). Cannot verify that this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli, nor confirm within-participant cue>control contrasts, whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps, or reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, or processing software. Therefore cannot confirm inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7. This is an fMRI empirical study of food (natural reward) cue-reactivity with within-participant contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results and adequate reporting (age/sex, cue type, scanner, software). However, it does not meet the review's stimulus modality requirement: cue presentation used personalized guided-imagery (auditory scripts) rather than visual stimuli. Therefore inclusion criterion I3 (use of visual stimuli) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I3.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cue-reactivity to visual natural rewards (erotic stimuli) in men seeking treatment for problematic pornography use. It reports within-participant cue-related contrasts (erotic vs control/non-reward cues), uses an ROI approach but also references whole-brain second-level contrasts (reported in Supplementary Figure S3), and provides participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), scanner field strength (3T), and processing/toolbox information (MATLAB, MarsBaR, WFU PickAtlas). The full article contains Introduction, Methods (including fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion; supplementary whole-brain results are referenced (acceptable per I6). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for core content (supplementary figures/tables may be separate).

Although this is an fMRI study of visual food cue (natural reward) reactivity with within-participant contrasts (high-calorie food > nonfood) and reports participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T) and processing software (SPM5), all core whole-brain task-evoked results appear to be reported using a predefined anatomical mask/regions-of-interest (insula and other food-related ROIs). The analyses and family-wise error corrections are described within that ROI mask; no unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or results are presented. Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and does not satisfy inclusion I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise map) or I6 (acceptable whole-brain reporting). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. It reports within-participant contrasts (LookSmoking > LookNeutral), and performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with corrected cluster thresholds; results are reported in tables and figures. Methods provide scanner field strength (Siemens Allegra 3.0T), processing software (SPM8; AlphaSim in AFNI), cue type (smoking/nicotine images), and participant characteristics (adults ≥18, Table 1). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food photographs) and reports within-subject contrasts (highly palatable > moderately palatable; high > neutral). The manuscript describes group-level whole-brain analyses (e.g., whole-brain probe analysis and references to Supporting Information Figure 1 and Table 1) and reports results in the main text. Participant age and sex (female, 18–25) and cue type (food) are reported; MRI acquisition and processing details are stated to be in Supporting Information. Core article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present in the provided full text (supplemental materials are acceptable to be separate). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for core content.

This is an fMRI study of smokers using visual, smoking-related stimuli (graphic cigarette warning labels) with within-subject contrasts of LABEL>CONTROL and HIGH>LOW. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholded and cluster-corrected) with tables/figures of peak coordinates. Participant age and sex are reported, cue type is nicotine-related (cigarette warnings), scanner field strength (3 T) and processing software (FSL) are specified. Although the stimuli are aversive/anti-smoking (graphic warnings) rather than appetitive drug cues, they are smoking-related visual cues and the study assesses craving change, so it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This study includes an fMRI cue-reactivity task using visual methamphetamine-related images and reports within-subject contrasts (MA cues > neutral cues). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment against criteria.

This is an fMRI study of smoking (drug) cue-reactivity using visual stimuli (videos/images) and reports within-subject contrasts of smoking cues > non-smoking cues. However, all reported activation results were derived from region-of-interest (ROI) analyses using an ROI mask (mOFC, VS, amygdala, hippocampus, ACC, insula); there is no unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map reported. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses) and does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain voxelwise group map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I6, I7. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual heroin-related cues (24 heroin-related vs 24 neutral images) with an event-related task and within-subject contrast heroin-related > neutral. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and post-hoc contrasts) are reported with correction (Monte Carlo) and regional results described in text/tables/figures. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not assess cue-reactivity to drug-related or natural reward-related cues in the sense required by the review. Specifically: (a) Exclusion IDs met: [] (no exclusion criteria triggered). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps are reported with cluster correction and coordinates), I6 (whole-brain results are reported as coordinates/figures described in text), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type — nicotine-related context, scanner field strength = 3T, processing software = FSL — are reported). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (the study tests neural/behavioral responses to FDA graphic warning labels — aversive public-health images — not typical drug-related or natural reward-related cue stimuli intended to elicit reward-related cue-reactivity), and I4 (while there is a within-subject contrast graphic>non-graphic, this does not correspond to a drug-cue > control drug-cue contrast as required). Thus, although the paper uses visual stimuli and reports whole-brain fMRI contrasts in nicotine users, its stimuli are anti-smoking warning images (aversive health images) rather than drug-related reward cues; it does not meet the core conceptual inclusion criteria I3/I4 for a cue-reactivity meta-analysis.”}]}]}]}

This study is excluded because it does not assess cue-reactivity to drug-related or specified natural reward cues. (a) Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses and cluster results) and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures with coordinates). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not assess drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual drug/food/sexual cues — it uses monetary probabilistic cues), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug-cues>control or natural-reward-cues>control), and I7 (although age/sex, scanner field strength, and software are reported, the cue type is monetary and not among the cue categories required by the review). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the core eligibility for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual natural-reward cues (food and sexual images) with first-year female participants. Methods report participant age/sex, cue types, scanner field strength (3T Philips), and processing software (SPM2). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; whole-brain results are provided). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be INCLUDED.

The provided full text appears to be a narrative review or overview (title, abstract, keywords, and metadata) rather than an original empirical fMRI study. There is no methods, participants, experimental design, or results reporting original human fMRI data or cue-reactivity contrasts. Thus it does not provide whole-brain task activation maps or within-participant cue>control contrasts. Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata present). Excluded under E6 (non-empirical paper).

This study uses fMRI with visual food cues (natural reward) and reports within-subject contrasts (fattening > non-fattening), and provides participant demographics and scanner/processing details. However, it does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map; analyses focus on extracting mean ROI z-scores and ROI-based group comparisons. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of natural reward visual cues), I4 (within-participant contrast fattening>non-fattening), I7 (reported age/sex, cue type=food, scanner field strength=3T, and processing software=FSL). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map reported) and consequently I6 (no whole-brain results provided in tables/figures/coordinates). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Given these facts, the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study tested cue-reactivity using visual natural (erotic) and monetary stimuli in 38 participants, and reports within-subject contrasts (monetary cue > control; erotic cue > control). Results are reported as whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates; SPM2 preprocessing is specified and scanner field strength (1.5T), participant age and sex (heterosexual males; mean age reported) are provided. therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used gustatory (taste) alcohol cues (alcohol vs. juice) rather than visual stimuli, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I3 requiring visual cue stimuli. Relevant inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-participant alcohol>control contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/figures), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails I3 (visual-stimulus requirement).

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual sexual stimuli (natural reward) with block-design cue exposure. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual drug-related cues (smoking/nicotine) with both smokers and non-smokers. This is an empirical fMRI study of natural reward (food) cue-reactivity using visual food images (I3).
