Thus it meets criteria I3 (fMRI of natural reward visual cues), I4 (within-participant contrasts of cue conditions with blurred control implicitly modeled), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described), and I7 (reported age/sex, cue type, field strength, software). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the meta-analysis requires fMRI cue-reactivity using visual stimuli. This study used an alcohol taste (gustatory) cue paradigm (Alcohol Taste > Water Taste); although brief visual labels preceded taste delivery, the primary cue modality was gustatory, not visual. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (within-subject Alcohol Taste>Water Taste contrast), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported with cluster correction), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described), and I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED due to I3 not met.

The study is an imaging investigation of intranasal insulin effects using arterial spin labeling (resting CBF) and includes behavioral ratings of food pictures outside the scanner. It does not present a within-participant cue>control task contrast (no fMRI during visual food-cue presentation) nor a task-evoked whole-brain activation map for food cues. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant characteristics, cue type = food, scanner field strength, and processing software are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI assessment of cue-reactivity to visual stimuli during scanning), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded from the meta-analysis which requires task-evoked visual cue-reactivity contrasts/maps.

This full-text reports an fMRI study of a natural reward (chocolate) using visual stimuli (chocolate vs neutral pictures) with within-participant contrasts (chocolate > neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (random-effects ANOVAs, F-maps, cluster thresholds). Whole-brain results are reported with coordinates/tables and figures. Participant information includes sex (34 females) and age is described (undergraduate students; Table 1 reported group characteristics), cue type (food/chocolate), MRI scanner field strength (3 T Siemens Magnetom Allegra), and processing software (BrainVoyager QX). The manuscript contains full Introduction/Methods/Results/Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3–I7 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual sexual cues (a natural reward) using pictures. It reports within-subject contrasts comparing sexual > neutral images (supraliminal and subliminal), and provides group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses using SPM5 with tables/figures/coordinates and standard voxelwise thresholds. Participant age/sex, cue type (sexual), MRI field strength (1.5T), and processing software are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study does not assess drug- or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli as required. It uses a monetary incentive delay task probing reward anticipation for monetary rewards (symbolic cues), not cue-reactivity to drug or natural reward images. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). (a) Exclusion criteria met: none. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables and text), I7 (participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (fMRI assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli) and I4 (within-participant contrast of drug cues>control stimuli or natural reward-related cues>control stimuli). Therefore exclude.

This is an fMRI study but it does not assess cue-reactivity with visual stimuli. It measured resting cerebral blood flow (ASL) 4 h after consumption of high- vs low-GI meals (physiologic manipulation), not responses to visual drug or natural reward-related cues. Exclusion rationale: No within-participant contrasts of cue>control (I4 not met); no task-evoked cue-reactivity paradigm with visual stimuli (I3 not met); although voxelwise comparisons were performed, they are meal-condition comparisons rather than task-evoked whole-brain cue maps (I5/I6 not met). Reporting of participant age/sex and scanner/software is present, but cue type (visual cue) is absent, so I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Conclusion: study does not meet the required inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity visual-stimulus fMRI studies and is excluded.

This article is a narrative review summarizing PET and fMRI findings rather than reporting original human fMRI experiments. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper/review without original human fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (not an original fMRI study assessing drug or natural reward-related cue-reactivity using visual stimuli), I4 (no within-participant contrast of drug cues > control stimuli reported as original analyses), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map from an original fMRI dataset), I7 (does not report participant-level details for an original fMRI sample). Full text is complete (contains introduction, discussion, and review of prior studies). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study does not meet key inclusion requirements for the review. While it includes within-participant contrasts of reward cues vs neutral (anticipation of gain/loss vs neutral) and reports participant sex/age information, cue type (monetary), scanner field strength (1.5T) and processing software (SPM5) (I4 and I7 met), it fails to meet I3 and I5/I6: the cues are monetary (secondary/monetary incentive) rather than the drug or primary natural reward cue types specified in the review scope, and the study did not acquire or report a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map (analyses focused on a ventral striatal ROI; authors state whole-brain images were not acquired). Therefore E3 (ROI-only / no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I5, I6. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not address the review’s target cue types. The meta-analysis focuses on fMRI cue-reactivity to drug or natural rewards (examples: nicotine, alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, heroin, food, sexual). This study uses monetary (secondary) reward anticipation (MID task) rather than drug or the natural reward cue types specified, so inclusion criterion I3 is not met. Likewise I7 is not met because the cue type is not among the listed reward categories required for eligibility, even though other details (age range, scanner field strength 1.5T, and processing software SPM8) are reported. The study does satisfy I4 (within-participant contrasts of reward cues > control), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for cue-reactivity fMRI using visual stimuli and reports only ROI-based hypothalamic results rather than whole-brain task activation maps. Exclusion ID met: E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion IDs met: I7 (reported participant age/sex, cue type: food, scanner field strength: 3.0T, and processing software: FSL). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (the fMRI paradigm did not assess visual cue-reactivity; the fMRI measured hypothalamic response to oral glucose ingestion, while visual/odorous food exposure occurred outside/during fasting rather than as an fMRI task), I4 (no within-participant contrast of visual food cues > control stimuli was performed in the fMRI data), I5 (no group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map was reported; imaging was limited to a single midsagittal slice and analyses used a manually defined hypothalamic ROI), I6 (not applicable because no whole-brain results were presented). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of anticipatory monetary reward using visual cues (gain vs neutral) in smokers and non-smokers, and reports participant age/sex, cue type (monetary), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI) — meeting I3, I4, and I7. However, the reported neuroimaging results are presented as ROI/small-volume-corrected analyses within a priori reward ROIs; no unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain results are reported. Therefore it does not meet I5 and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

This study meets I3 (fMRI study of reward-related cue-reactivity using visual monetary cues in a MID task), I4 (within-participant contrasts of gain>neutral were performed), I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). However, I7 is not satisfied in the provided full text: participant sex is reported (9 males, 10 females) but participant age (mean or range) is not explicitly reported in the supplied content (Table 1 is referenced but its contents are not present here). Because I7 requires relevant information regarding participant age and sex, and age is not available in the provided document, the study does not meet all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The full text appears otherwise complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is false. Given the missing age information in the provided material, I exclude the study from the meta-analysis dataset.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol cues (drug-related) with within-participant contrasts (alcohol > neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain results are reported with cluster-level thresholding and coordinates (Table 2) and figures. Methods report scanner field strength (Philips 3T) and processing software (BrainVoyager QX); participant demographics and age comparisons are referenced (Table 1), and cue type (alcohol) is explicit. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (visual drug cue fMRI, within-participant contrasts, whole-brain group maps, coordinate reporting, and relevant methodological details).

This is a resting-state fMRI pharmacological study of acute naltrexone effects on intrinsic functional connectivity, not a task-based cue-reactivity study. It does not present any drug- or natural-reward visual cue task, nor any within-participant cue>control contrast or whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (not a cue-reactivity visual-stimulus fMRI study), I4 (no within-participant cue>control contrast), I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I6 (not applicable—no task-based whole-brain results to report), I7 (while age/sex/scanner/software are reported, cue type and task details are not provided). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without whole-brain task activation). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion reason (E4): This study reports resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses and does not include any task-evoked fMRI cue-reactivity contrast. Inclusion met: I7 (participant age/sex, cue type = food, MRI field strength = 3.0T, and processing software SPM8 are reported). Inclusion not met: I3 (no fMRI task assessing cue-reactivity with visual stimuli during scanning — images were presented after scanning), I4 (no within-participant task contrast of cues>control), I5 (no task-evoked, whole-brain group-level activation map). Therefore the paper must be excluded under E4.

This is an fMRI study of alcohol (beer) cue-reactivity using visual cues (abstract shapes predicting beer vs water). It reports within-subject contrasts (beer>water) for anticipation (cue+delay), outcome notification, and delivery phases. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (T-maps, cluster-level FWE correction) and coordinates are provided; maps are available online. Key metadata are reported (participant age and sex, cue type: alcohol, 3T scanner, SPM8 processing). Full text includes Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete.

This article is a narrative review (non-empirical) summarizing neuroimaging studies and does not report original human fMRI task data. Exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical papers without original human fMRI data) applies. No inclusion criteria are met: I3 (an original fMRI study assessing cue-reactivity with visual stimuli) is not met; I4 (within-participant drug-cue>control contrast) is not met; I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) is not met; I6 (reporting of whole-brain results) is not met; I7 (reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner strength, processing software) is not met for an original dataset. Additionally, the provided full text is incomplete (abstract/introduction/references only), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a visual cue-reactivity task presenting alcohol, marijuana, polydrug, and appetitive (food, faces, landscapes) images and neutral controls. Within-subject contrasts comparing each cue type to neutral (e.g., alcohol>neutral, appetitive>neutral) are reported. Group-level, mixed-effects whole-brain analyses with cluster-based thresholding are described for the cue reactivity task, satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise reporting (thresholding and group maps described; results presented in text/figures). Required study details are provided: participant age and sex (mean age 18.92, 19 females), cue types, MRI scanner field strength (3.0T Siemens Magnetom Trio), and processing software (FSL v5.0). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual alcohol advertisements as cues with a within-subject ALCOHOL > CONTROL contrast. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses (ALCOHOL > CONTROL) with cluster-level multiple comparison correction and provides peak coordinates, tables, and figures. Participant demographics (age range and sex distribution), cue type (alcohol), scanner field strength (3.0T), and processing software (SPM8; AFNI’s 3dClustSim used for cluster correction) are all reported. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental materials are referenced but not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task study using visual e-cigarette advertising images (nicotine-related cues) and reports within-participant contrasts of e-cigarette > neutral images. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxelwise t-tests with cluster correction) were conducted and reported (tables/figures/supplement). Participant age and sex, cue type (nicotine/e-cigarette), MRI field strength (3T), and processing software (AFNI) are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3–I7 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual natural reward cues (food images). It reports within-subject contrasts (food vs. non-food; high-calorie vs. non-food) and group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM8 on 3.0T data. Results are reported with figures/tables and SVC/FWE-corrected voxelwise statistics within ROIs; whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses were performed and described. Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength, and processing software are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3–I7) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual cues of natural reward (appetizing and disgusting food images) and reports within-participant contrasts (appetizing > bland/nonfood, disgusting > bland/nonfood) at the group (random-effects) level. Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were performed with results reported as statistical maps and peak coordinates; coordinates and thresholding are reported in text (and supplemental tables), and figures show activation overlays. Participant age and sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM99) are all reported. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for visual cue-reactivity fMRI studies of natural rewards and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using visual food cues (pictures of candy/dessert) and within-subject contrasts. The task modeled food cue conditions relative to a low-level baseline (fixation) and conducted group-level, whole-brain second-level one-sample t-tests and factorial contrasts (e.g., LATER vs NOW, conditions vs baseline). Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported with coordinates and figures. Relevant participant details (age, sex), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T), and processing software (SPM8) are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting, not non-empirical).

This is an fMRI study of nicotine (smoking) cue-reactivity using pictorial visual stimuli. It includes a within-subject contrast reflecting drug cues vs control (LCSP minus LCNP) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects RM-ANOVA and between-group t-tests) with reported coordinates and cluster results (Table 1 and figures). Results are reported using SPM8 on a 3T scanner; participant age and sex are provided. Although results use small-volume correction within a priori ROIs, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses were performed and coordinates/cluster statistics are reported, satisfying the meta-analysis reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without task effect, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using visual food cues (natural reward) with within-participant contrasts (food > nonfood; high-calorie > nonfood) fulfilling I3 and I4. However, the reported results are restricted to predefined ROIs using small-volume FWE correction; the paper does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or whole-brain results, so it fails I5 and thus meets exclusion E3 (only ROI-based results reported). Additionally, the full text as provided does not clearly report participant sex (I7 not verifiable from text). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED due to E3 (and missing I5/I7).

Provided "full text" is incomplete (a redirect/metadata page only). Core article content (methods, results) is not present, so I cannot verify key inclusion criteria. Cannot confirm that this is an fMRI cue-reactivity study using visual stimuli (I3), that it reports within-participant contrasts of cues>control (I4), that it includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps (I5/I6), or that participant/cue/scanner/software details are reported (I7). Therefore the study cannot be assessed for inclusion and is excluded due to incomplete full text preventing verification of all inclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used visual cues (participant-supplied photographs of the rejecting beloved vs a familiar neutral face) and reports a within-subject contrast (rejecter > neutral). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and whole-brain exploratory results are reported (thresholded at P<0.001 uncorrected) with coordinates/tables described in the text and tables. Participant age and sex are reported (mean age 19.8, 10 women/5 men), cue type (romantic/partner images, a natural reward-related cue), scanner field strength (1.5 T), and processing software (SPM2) are all provided. Although ROI analyses are emphasized, whole-brain task-evoked results are also reported, so the study is not excluded for ROI-only reporting. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward (food) using visual/abstract cues (basket images), with within-subject contrasts comparing high vs no food reward (10 SP vs 0 SP). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected results and supplementary tables/figures) and ROI plus whole-brain results. Participant demographics (age ranges, sex matching), cue type (food), scanner field strength (3T Tim Trio), and processing software (SPM8) are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of natural reward-related (food) cue reactivity using visual stimuli in humans. It reports within-subject contrasts of food-related stimuli (high/low caloric food blocks) relative to baseline and examines changes across conditions (glucose vs. water) and timepoints. Group-level whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses were conducted using SPM8 and whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures (clusters, coordinates, and thresholding). Participant age/sex, cue type (food), scanner field strength (3.0 T), and processing software (SPM8) are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). Hence the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI cue-reactivity study of alcohol that meets several inclusion criteria (within-participant alcohol>control contrast; group-level, voxelwise analysis with reported peak coordinates; reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, scanner field strength, and processing software). However, it does NOT meet I3 because the cue modality is gustatory (alcohol taste vs litchi juice) rather than visual stimuli, and the meta-analysis specifically requires visual cue paradigms. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to visual-stimulus cue-reactivity studies.
